text: The Iranians are troubled by the possibility that the US will take over the island of Kharj - from where Iran exports 90% of its oil. text: The ceremony of stopping the clock in the Kidnapped Square 📌 Tuesday | 27.01.26 | 17:30 | The Kidnapped Square The Kidnapped Square, which was a home for families and the center of activity for the families' headquarters, became a place of pilgrimage for the amazing Israelis who came to support the families and the struggle. author: BringThemHomeNow
text: Farewell to Rani Goili 🎗️ The Goili family, the Israel Police and the headquarters of the families of the abductees announce the return to burial of our beloved Major Rani Goili, who died in a heroic battle, was kidnapped on the morning of the seventh of October and returned after 843 days in captivity.   The funeral will take place today, January 28, at the Mitar cemetery.  At 10:30 the funeral procession will start from Shura camp. The convoy will accompany the coffin of the late Major Rani Goili, until the Miter settlement via road 431, onto road 6 at the Nesher interchange and through road 60. The public is invited to come and stand with flags on the sides of the road and pay Rani a final respect.  Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

author: BringThemHomeNow
text: "In the first days after the Black Day, the families of the abductees settled on Kaplan Street. I was the only one stationed at the square with 3 signs. With the passage of time, the square became the heart of the families of the abductees and the heart of the people." Danny Miren, the father of the POW survivor Amri Miran, arrived today for the last Shabbat reception in the square of the abductees, with his son, daughter-in-law and granddaughters by his side, and told about those early days: "Last Shabbat reception in the square of the abductees. Rani, the last of the kidnapped, is at home. Allow me to thank the IDF soldiers and all the security forces who stand guard day and night. I would also like to thank all the people who continued to support and be with us. With Rani's return, we and the entire nation can take deep breaths from the air of the good country. and put a smile on your face.  From here I appeal to all the people of Israel, let us not stop the struggle for the things that are important to all of us: mainly.- The struggle for a reformed state, in which there will be respect for all government institutions, a state that respects and cares for all its residents, a state where equality will be a supreme value, a state where we respect one another, despite differences of opinion.  A country with concern for future generations. They deserve a better country.   The current generation, the warrior, has proven itself beyond all expectations. About this youth it is impossible to say what was said in the past: "This is this youth...." And a final request - for the purpose of commemorating and leaving a legacy for future generations, we will leave the square as a memory. We'll leave the place named "kidnapped square". Assign us a place in the square, where we will erect a monument, on which we will hang all the washers and pins." Photo credit: Uriel Ibn Sapir, Alon Gilboa Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

author: BringThemHomeNow
text: "Yesterday I visited Nahal Oz, at home. This is the fourth time since I was released, but this time was a little different. There is no one of our own across the fence." Captive survivor Amri Miren stood moved today at the last Shabbat reception in the Kidnapped Square and shared his feelings with the large crowd since the return of Rani, the last kidnapped: "For 843 days you fought here for the return of 255 kidnapped. You fought for the values. In memory of the fallen and the murdered and above all so that our children will have a better world.   I am proud to be part of this nation. I am proud to be part of the Nahal Oz community that founded and led the Shabbat receptions in the square for two years. i am proud I am proud but also with fear of what the next day will bring. Or rather today is already here. The day we longed for.   And today, especially today I want to remind us, all of us, that even in order to get up and recover, we need to be together. we must be together Do everything to make it better here.  For the sake of the country, for our sake, in memory of the many murdered, in memory of the fallen without whom we would not be here. And above all for the sake of future generations.   I want to take the opportunity that I stand here before you and thank you. To our heroic soldiers and the servants of the security system, even in these moments, they sacrifice their souls and bodies so that we can stand here.  To the bereaved families who gave the most precious of all.  To every Nahal Oz community for generations.  to the headquarters of the families and to the square that were a second home for my family.  To thank you dear people - that you didn't stop, that you didn't give up and continued to do things each in his own way and in his own faith." @LishayLM Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

author: BringThemHomeNow
text: Exactly one year ago Or Levy, Ohad Ben Ami, and Eli Sharabi crossed the border and returned home. Through tears, we watched them fall into the arms of their loved ones.     Since then, we’ve watched them begin to piece their lives back together, bravely sharing some of the ordeals they endured in the hell of Gaza.    Almost immediately, they joined the fight to bring the rest home, until the last hostage.    Their strength and courage helped unite the Israeli people and supporters around the world.    Now that there are no hostages left in Gaza, our work continues.  We must help them heal.  We must help all the families heal.  We must help our people heal.    Now, we rise. 💛  Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

author: BringThemHomeNow
text: "I am Talik Goili, the proud mother of Ran, a YSM police officer, the first to leave and the last to return." With these words, Talik opened the eulogy over the fresh grave of her son, the late Israeli hero Ran Goili: "Rani, I imagine you up there on the tribune with all the heroes of the kingdom, with all the heroes who sacrificed their lives.  I imagine you bringing everyone together and telling them - you have to come hear my obituaries, it will be cool. I imagine all of you on the tribune - all heroes of the Resurrection War.   Shortly after you were kidnapped, they invited all the families of the abductees to a meeting in Ra'anana, a rainy day, my father and I leave the house, highway 6 and suddenly the rain stops, and a huge, huge rainbow appears. We drive to her right inside the arch, look at her in silence and she accompanies us until one moment we entered her and then she disappeared. And I knew it was a sign from you. I just wanted to tell you my beloved child that the hope that you might come back to us with two legs and maybe even one is what gave us the strength to get through this long period without you.   During this whole period we talked about you endlessly, it seems that you became everyone's child. My beloved Rani, I assure you that it was thanks to you that we remembered with Israel that despite the differences we are one great and strong nation.   You came out to protect everyone and they all deserve your sacrifice. 700 soldiers searched for you, found you, brought you back. There is no such nation in the world.  I'm talik guili, proud mother proud. And thank you for being here, seeing you at every intersection with the flags all along the way is so exciting and empowering. You have no idea. I don't know how we would have gotten through the whole two years and four months without you, thank you." Photo credit: Paulina Fatimer, Uriel Ibn Sapir Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

author: BringThemHomeNow
text: After over two years of fighting for the return of the abductees, 254 of the 255 abductees who were in Gaza were resettled on the seventh of October. This evening, hundreds of volunteers and employees of the headquarters of the families for the return of the abductees gathered together with the families of the abductees and returnees for an event in recognition of their part in this value struggle.   The headquarters of the families for the return of the abductees was one of the most significant and moral civil organizations in Israel's history. Tens of thousands of Israelis and Jews from the Diaspora volunteered and contributed their time and ability to a clear goal - the return of all the abductees, alive and dead, home, some for rehabilitation and some for burial. This evening gathered many of those who joined the struggle, volunteers from all over the country from those standing at the intersections, diplomatic advisors, producers, field workers, speakers, photographers, logistics, kitchen and warehouse workers, the resilience and legal teams, family companions, advertising, social, creative and more. In order to thank and cherish the dedicated workers and volunteers, hundreds of members of the families of the abductees and the survivors of the captivity came who learned about the activities of the family headquarters while in Gaza and after their release. In the crowd were many family members and survivors of captivity who came to say thank you to the hundreds of people who put their lives on hold to save them and bring them back.   The headquarters has changed its face in the last month and continues the fight with a dedicated team together with the Guili family to recover the last kidnapped Ran Guili. Taliq and Shira Goili, Rani's mother and sister, represented the family and thanked the volunteers and workers who continue to help in every possible way.    Tlik, Rani's mother, thanked the large crowd: "I want to thank you on my behalf, on behalf of my family, Rani's friends from the neighborhood, from the unit, thank you for being here. When Rani went out on the seventh of October to Otef, to a party, to the unknown, he did not check who he was saving. He didn't care about religion, race and gender or political opinion, neither do you. All that stood and stands before your eyes is that Rani needs and must return, for us, for you and for the home of all of us.   Like my Rani, you left everything to help those who needed the help, those who needed their voice to be heard. You reminded us what it means to be good people in the middle of the road when you only saw a person in front of you with no past, present or future deposits, without asking questions other than how to help.  To the families of the 254 abductees who returned and returned some for rehabilitation and some for burial, thank you for being and you are to us as a family, thank you for being with us until the last abductee, thank you that you also see Bernie as you. author: BringThemHomeNow
text: Further to the publications regarding an initiated campaign that was allegedly carried out against the POW coordinator, Gal Hirsch: The headquarters of the families of the abductees was concerned from day one with only one thing and that was the return of 255 abductees home. The headquarters acted all along according to a clear strategy - a determined and persistent struggle, in Israel and around the world, in order to return our brothers and sisters home, some for rehabilitation and some for eternal rest.   We regret that there are those who prefer to spread false claims.  The headquarters never engaged, either directly or indirectly, in order to discredit Gal Hirsch, did not initiate any such campaign and certainly did not spend a single shekel on a campaign that did not exist.   After two and a half years of activity, the headquarters closes its activities after having fully achieved the goal of its establishment - all 255 abductees were returned to Israel. author: BringThemHomeNow
text: The story of the families headquarters for the return of the abducted and missing - the family team The family team was the beating heart of the families, a source of warmth, comfort and unconditional love. The team connected the families with the professionals, maintained direct and daily contact with them and constituted a central address for the families for any need.  The team leaders accompanied, coordinated and supported the families while responding to their needs, coordinated between parties at the headquarters and outside, assisted in the preparation for formal and informal meetings, delegations abroad for leaders and government officials in Israel and around the world.  The families know how to tell about the endless support and generosity of the team members. They were a reason and an incentive to get up in the morning even on dark days. With their help, the helplessness of many families turned into a sense of ability, despair into hope and sorrow and loneliness into companionship and comfort.   Thanks to the accompanying families and their ability to connect family members from all sectors with women and professionals from all types and fields to provide assistance in any field and interest. In this way, it was possible for the families to maintain both their dignity and their unique voice, and also to place it at the center of the public struggle for the return of their loved ones in Israel and around the world. And Dalia added: "Rani is the values ​​we are fighting for, so there is no rehabilitation and no transition to the next stages as long as the mission is not completed and Rani is not at home."

author: BringThemHomeNow
text: Yesterday Uri Danino was supposed to celebrate his 27th birthday, but he will forever remain 25. Uri was born on January 31, 1999 in Jerusalem, the son of Einav and Elhanan. He was the brother of Isaac, David, Aaron and Hodia. Uri was an especially loved person, with a big heart and lots of friends, someone who was always there for others, at any hour.  Uri loved nature and field trips, spending time with friends and living the moment. Black coffee was almost a hobby for him, and those who knew him spoke of a man who radiates joy in life, kindness and mutual guarantee. He planned to start studying electrical engineering, and he had dreams and plans for the future.  On October 7, 2023 Uri was at the Nova party. He was already on his way to safety, but chose to turn back, into the fire, to save lives. Uri rescued Mia and Iti Regev and Omar Shem Tov in his car, but on their way they were ambushed by terrorists, and they were all kidnapped to Gaza.  Uri was held captive by Hamas for about 11 months. Even in the most impossible conditions, he continued to show responsibility, courage and concern for others, and fought so that his wounded friends would receive treatment.  On August 29, 2024, the late Uri Danino was brutally murdered by Hamas terrorists, in a tunnel in the Rafah area, along with Carmel Gat, Hersh Goldberg-Poulin, Aden Yerushalmi, Alex Lobnov and the late Almog Sarosi.  Today, we will stop for a moment and remember Uri, a young man who, in the moment of truth, chose not to save only himself, but to go back to save others. This choice defines who he was, and the values ​​he left behind.  In his memory 💔 Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

author: BringThemHomeNow
text: The story of the headquarters of the families for the return of the kidnapped and the missing - the business sector desk The business sector team was established as a strategic and executive arm of the headquarters, and succeeded in harnessing hundreds of organizations, managers and CEOs to an active partnership in the struggle. Behind about 700 companies stood people with a big heart and a clear moral compass, who were involved in driving complex moves and leading large-scale initiatives.   The team was a catalyst for resource mobilization, created a continuous presence of the abductee issue within the companies, and ensured broad public awareness - from giant signs, conferences and supermarket shelves to trains, employee screens, gas stations and other public spaces. The team connected the needs of the families with the capabilities and resources of the business sector, and turned relationships into partnerships and actual actions.   In addition, the team established and will operate the site for donations and the distribution of struggle products, we created boxes and products that translated identification into action. The site was a significant source of funding for the headquarters' activities, combining content, emotion and meaning with practical action that motivates action and creates a real impact.  Over 3 million stolen pins 🎗️ were sold and worn everywhere by members of the media and the general public.  In the photos: huge signs hung on office buildings across the country to highlight and emphasize the issue of abductees in the public space. To mark two years on October 7, hundreds of companies, municipalities, councils, academic institutions and businesses changed their logo to a yellow logo to express and call out the issue of the abductees on social networks. Photo from the visit of the vice presidents of human resources to the families' headquarters. The Rosh Hashanah package was purchased by businesses and private individuals, and it is possible to continue to carry out the activities of the headquarters for the release of all the abductees. author: BringThemHomeNow
text: Tomorrow, Friday, we will have the first Shabbat without abductees in Gaza with the kibbutz movement, the Kibbutz Tzva community, the families of the abductees, survivors of captivity and all the people of Israel who returned the abductees home.   At the end of the week when the last abductee was resettled, and the 843rd of October was the first day since 2014 when there are no more Israelis abducted in Gaza, join us for the reception of the last Shabbat 💛 📌 Friday | 30.1 | 13:00 | Kidnapped Square, Tel Aviv after a long struggle, 255 of our brothers and sisters were returned home, for rehabilitation and burial. Although this is a powerful event that warms the heart, our heart is not whole, we do not forget that 87 martyrs were returned, of which 46 were murdered by Hamas. 46 abductees whose families could embrace and not bury. While Rani's family sits seven, in motion The kibbutz promise to remember and remember the heroism of the late Major Ran Gueli who fell in the battle on Kibbutz Alumim on October 7 and was 24 years old when he died.  💛🙏💛 The kibbutzim, led by Kibbutz Nahal Oz, led the Shabbat receptions in the square during 120 consecutive weeks together with the headquarters of the families of the abductees. Hundreds of families of abductees, survivors of captivity, Israeli artists and the public in Israel participated in these events. In total, about 2 million Israelis participated in the Shabbat receptions of the kibbutz movement, who supported and took part in identification and solidarity with the struggle until they were all restored.  Join us for the last time for sure Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

author: BringThemHomeNow
text: "Rani, I didn't write anything because I always speak from the heart with what I feel at that moment." Itzik, the father of Israel's hero and "Defender of the Unknowns" Major Ran Gueli, the late, now said goodbye to his son: "What you did, saved and united, is not something that is taken for granted. And I want to say that every day we find something new about you.   A few hours ago we got you on the line. We opened the closet and touched you, kissed you. After two and a half years you are completely whole.  Rani was the 250th body in the excavations. 250 in Gematria is Ran, this is another one of the things we received from you, it's as if you arrange everything for us from above.   The whole nation of Israel and the whole world know your story, everyone embraces you, you are everyone's child. I am so proud to be your father.  I miss you every second, and every minute, love you, love you, miss you.   Thank you very much to everyone for the respect you give him, it's an honor for him and not for us - thank you.'  Photo credit: Paulina Petimer Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

author: BringThemHomeNow
text: "On the day I returned home, the clock in the square showed 738 days. Since then another 106 days have passed in which I could stand by your side and be part of the most important value and moral struggle that has ever been here."  Standing excitedly, with his fellow captives by his side, POW survivor Segev Kalfon told today about the first time he saw from the tunnels of Gaza an image of the abductees' square in the center of which stood the stopwatch counting the 'kidnapped time' in days, minutes and seconds: "That's exactly how we felt, how every minute is eternity and every second could be the last second we breathe. That's how the families of all 255 abductees also felt, that every second is eternity. When I saw your pictures from the square, standing here supporting our families, you were our light and our hope, and no less than that - it's time to say thank you to all those who fought here and to all the soldiers who went out to fight for us, I only learned about the struggle for our return, I saw them everywhere Yellow chairs. I saw what you did for us. Stopping the clock is a defining moment, but it marks the end of one, critical phase in which all 255 abductees are no longer held by the abominable Hamas. Now the 87 families of the abductees will be able to evacuate together with us, the survivors of the captivity. Thank you and you. Now get up."  Photo credit: Paulina Fatimer, Lior Rothstein Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

author: BringThemHomeNow
text: The story of the family headquarters for the return of the kidnapped and missing - diplomacy and international missions The international department led one of the largest and most significant international moves in the history of the State of Israel. The department included hundreds of employees and volunteers, among them diplomats, former ambassadors, former MKs, academics and media, and field staffs in 50 countries. As part of the international diplomatic and legal work, hundreds of delegations of families of abductees and survivors of captivity went out, mainly to the USA and key European countries, with the aim of making their voices heard and influencing policy. Members of the families met with presidents, prime ministers, foreign ministers, elected officials and officials Key in the international arena, and reached the decision-making centers in Washington, New York, London, Berlin, Paris, Brussels, Geneva and The Hague. Each delegation was accompanied by extensive communication, careful logistical planning and close coordination in Israel and abroad. the lives and the spaces, and changed the public discourse in the country. The peak of the effort was recorded in the meetings held by President Trump with the survivors of the captivity and the family members and in the speeches given by the special envoy Witkoff, Trump's son-in-law Kushner and his daughter Ivanka in the Kidnapped Square in front of half a million participants.  Along with the many trips, many meetings of the families of the abductees and the returnees with diplomats and government officials from dozens of countries around the world were held at the headquarters and in the square. author: BringThemHomeNow
text: The story of the families headquarters for the return of the abducted and missing - the family team The family team was the beating heart of the families, a source of warmth, comfort and unconditional love. The team connected the families with the professionals, maintained direct and daily contact with them and constituted a central address for the families for any need.  The team leaders accompanied, coordinated and supported the families while responding to their needs, coordinated between parties at the headquarters and outside, assisted in the preparation for formal and informal meetings, delegations abroad for leaders and government officials in Israel and around the world.  The families know how to tell about the endless support and generosity of the team members. They were a reason and an incentive to get up in the morning even on dark days. With their help, the helplessness of many families turned into a sense of ability, despair into hope and sorrow and loneliness into companionship and comfort.   The family team also included the family support system. Dozens of volunteer attendants who worked day and night to help families.  Thanks to the accompanying families and their ability to connect family members from all sectors with women and professionals of all types and fields to provide assistance in any field and interest, it was possible for families to maintain both their dignity and their unique voice, and also to place it at the center of the public struggle for the return of their loved ones in Israel and around the world.  The escorts, escorts and family staff became members of the family of the abductees, most of them remained in touch even with the return of their loved ones and some of them even continue to accompany the survivors of the captivity. author: BringThemHomeNow
text: With the recovery of all the hijackers we end the current activity of our page. After almost 28 months of non-stop struggle, day and night, we stop, take a breath and ask to say thank you. Thank you from the deepest place in my heart.  To each and every one of you who stood by the families. who refused to get used to it. who refused to give up. who refused to normalize.  who chose again and again not to look away.  You were with us in moments when the pain was greater than words. You echoed the cries. You bore the names. You gave way to tears, and also to the rare moments of light, when a small crack of hope finally appeared.  Anyone who took part in the struggle to return the abductees, is not just a supporter. He is part of history. Part of the most moral and valuable civil struggle that the State of Israel has known since its establishment.  You embraced the families as if they were your own. You carried them when they no longer had the strength left to carry themselves. And when it seemed like the world was moving on, you stayed.  Your likes. Your comments. Your shares. The words you wrote at two in the morning.  These were never small gestures.  They were a lifeline. They were a breath in the dark. They were evidence that even in the heart of the nightmare, humanity does not disappear. she struggles she is standing She illuminates.  One day they will ask: "Where were you during this time?"  And you can say, I was there. I was not silent. I didn't turn my back. I was part of the force that brought them home.  Thank you for carrying us when we ran out of air. Thank you for not giving up. Thank you for choosing Or.  You will always be a part of our hearts. And we will forever be grateful to you 💛 Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

author: BringThemHomeNow
text: The story of the headquarters of the families for the return of the abducted and the missing - strategy The level of struggle and the strategic consultation formed the core of the activities of the headquarters of the families of the abductees. Leading women and professionals in their fields, of a variety of ages and professional experience, veteran Israelis and new immigrants served on the floor.  The chief strategist together with the strategic consulting team formulated the policy of the headquarters, managed and carried out dozens of studies to form public perceptions in Israel and abroad, examined the extent to which the headquarters met the goals and objectives set for it by the families of the abductees and adapted the strategy to target audiences, sectors and policy makers around the world.   The strategic team included experts in the fields of media, international, religious, ultra-Orthodox, Knesset and government, Arab countries and international law.  The headquarters of the families of the abductees was run through its democratically authorized institutions. Strategic decisions were made by majority vote by the plenum of representatives of the families of the abductees, while the implementation of the policy decided upon was entrusted to the faithful hands of the assembly - a limited selection of representatives from among the families.  The headquarters operated one of the largest, most sophisticated and versatile content, media, data and advertising systems that have operated in Israel since time immemorial.   At the beginning of its journey, the headquarters was assisted by external offices, but as of April 2024, an independent advertising, creative, media purchasing, production, post-production and ideation system was built at the headquarters. Senior women and men of the advertising world worked alongside talented and young talents to manage an unprecedented advertising campaign in Israel and abroad.  In the field of information, Israeli communication teams, international communication and the social department worked at the headquarters. Elite units of information that handled the aggregate of tens of thousands of inquiries from the media in Israel and around the world. The departments initiated media exposure in accordance with the strategy of the headquarters and in accordance with the events that accompanied us from the October 7th until the return of the last abductee. The social network established collaborations with the most powerful media organizations and leading platforms. The department was a cutting edge of creativity and groundbreaking thinking in all fields.  Photographs: The Seventh Day of Iron Swords (credit Rani Graff) 02.01.2025 Painting buildings yellow. (credit Gili Chen | Doron Saar Highlapse - A new Perspective of Moments) 16.09.2025 - on Gaza Street in front of the Prime Minister's house (credit HQ of the kidnapped families) 01.2026 - strategy team meeting with the Guli family in a family room in the squar

author: BringThemHomeNow
text: Today Rani Goili should have celebrated his 27th birthday, but he will forever remain 24 years old. Rani was born on February 11, 1999. Ben Latlik and Itzik Goili, a younger brother to Omari. Shira later joined and Rennie was awarded the title of "big brother". Ketam and Luna, Rani's favorite boxers, have always been part of the family.  From his childhood, Rani was a rare combination of tenderness and strength, sensitivity and responsibility, joy of life and a sense of mission. A young and dignified man who always spoke at the level of the poor with a powerful and calm presence. Rani liked to play the guitar, ride motorcycles and exercise. He was always surrounded by a large circle of friends, true friends who stood by each other, one for the other.  From his youth, Rani knew that he wanted to serve in a significant role and when he enlisted in the IDF, he volunteered to serve in the Golani Brigade, where he stood out as a brave, dedicated and purposeful fighter. After his release from the IDF, he chose to continue serving, and enlisted in the Israel Police. He served as a fighter in the Negev YSM unit in the southern district and passed the tests for the army, however, due to his young age, he had to wait until he was 25. During his service, he stood out for his courage, coolness and extraordinary dedication to the safety of the citizens.  On the morning of October 7th, Rani was injured at home with a fractured shoulder following a motorcycle accident, but as soon as he heard about the infiltration of the terrorists, he put on a uniform and went out to help his friends from the unit in fighting. During that morning, Rani led dozens of survivors of the Nova festival to safety, and later joined the fighters and the standby squad of Kibbutz Alumim who tried to stop the dozens of terrorists who tried to infiltrate the kibbutz. Rani fought with strength and ferocity at the front of the battle at the entrance to the kibbutz and after a stubborn battle, and only after he ran out of ammunition, Rani fell in battle and was kidnapped to Gaza.  Today, let's pause for a moment and all of us remember Major Ran Goyili, a hero of Israel and a 'defender of the unknown', the one with the big smile and the broad shoulders. The sociable guy, funny and loved by his friends. A huge heart, a true friend, one who always saw those who were left behind, and was the first to lend a hand. In his memory 💔 Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

text: Today Itai Chen should have celebrated his 22nd birthday, but he will forever remain 19 years old. Itai was born on February 2, 2004, the second son of Ruby and Hagit Chen and a younger brother to Roy. Later he got to be a big brother to Alon.  Itay grew up in Netanya and was a promising athlete. He liked to play basketball, climb climbing walls and travel around the country. When he got to high school he studied in the excellence class.   As a teenager, Itai was involved in social activities and was a youth leader. Although he was injured during his duty as an instructor, he insisted on continuing in the role. During the long vacation, Itay worked as an instructor at a summer camp at Tel Aviv University, where he met Netta Simon, who became his partner.   In August 2022, Itai enlisted as an armored fighter in the 77th Battalion of the glorious 7th Brigade.   On the morning of October 7th, I went out with the members of the tank team with him to fight the many terrorists who infiltrated the Nahal Oz sector. The team fought for hours, shot, ran over and stopped waves of terrorists, while constantly moving between different points, thus saving many lives. The traces of the tank's journey left on the ground were silent testimony to the team's initiative and determined fighting. Thanks to their fierce fighting, together with other heroes, they managed to prevent more crowds of terrorists from reaching Nahal Oz, Kibbutz Sa'ad, Kfar Gaza, and the main road.  Sergeant Itai Chen fell during the heroic battle and was kidnapped. Along with him were also kidnapped the tank commander, Capt. Daniel Peretz, the 14th, and the survivor of the captivity, Maj. Gen. Matan Engrest. The late Sergeant Tomer Leibovitz, a member of the fourth team, also fell in the heroic battle that morning.  Today, we will stop for a moment and we will all remember Itai, the Lion King, who loved the State of Israel and fell in battle to protect its citizens. The heroic warrior with a heart of gold, who gave of himself to all.  In his memory 💔 @EmailRubychen @hagitchen Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

author: BringThemHomeNow
text: This month Almog Sarousi should have celebrated his 29th birthday, but he will forever remain 27 years old. Almog was born on January 18, 1997, the first son of Nira Vigal. Over the years he also became an elder brother to Amit, Lahav and Shaked.  From a young age Almog excelled in everything he did - from studies to football and karate classes. Almog also had a great love for music. He played the classical and electric guitar as well as the drums, and would sit with his family and friends holding the guitar and charming everyone. Together with his friends Alon Verber, who was murdered on Black Sabbath, and Guy Iloz, who was kidnapped and murdered in Gaza, the three rented an urban shelter and used it as a music studio and gyms.  When he reached the age of 18, Almog enlisted in the Givat patrol and finished his service as an outstanding fighter. He always said that the army gave him a real sense of meaning and mission in life and that this period earned him many values ​​and friends for life.  Almog loved to travel. Together with 'Miko' (his Suzuki Jimny Jeep) he plowed the country from north to south, and saw the world in his travels in the United States, throughout Europe, Africa and the Far East. When he went on a trip to India, Almog met Shahar Gindi, the love of his life.  Almog and Shahar were together for three and a half years. They lived in Ariel, where they studied at university (Almog Civil Engineering and Shahar Psychology) and both had to start their last school year. Almog had already planned the marriage proposal.  Almog's real dream was to engage in education and open a daycare center for at-risk youth, in addition he dreamed of settling in the Negev/Golan and developing these places befitting a true Zionist. "There is nothing better than being good" was his motto and he acted according to it. He gave private math lessons for free to boys who came from hard-to-find families, he would collect money from his friends and go buy a holiday meal for needy families, he volunteered at the "Yadidis" association.  On October 7, 2023 Almog was at the Nova party together with Shahar and a few other friends. They tried to escape by car, but a squad of Hamas terrorists ambushed them and shot at them. Almog was wounded by the shooting and those who were with him in the car were murdered, among them: Omri Achrak, Noam Shai, Daniel Waldman and his lover Shahar, whom he tried to save, and remained by her side until the moment he was kidnapped.  Almog survived in Hamas captivity for 11 months. Despite the impossible conditions Almog managed to recover from his wounds and survive bravely. Arabic studies in high school helped him during his time in captivity. Throughout the whole period his spirit did not break and he remained brave, strong, optimistic and full of hope.  On August 29, 2024, Almog was brutally murdered by Hamas terrorists, along with his friends Carmel Gat, Hersh Goldberg-Polin, Eden Yerushalmi, Alex Lubnov and the late Uri Danino. Tod

author: BringThemHomeNow
text: For the first time since 2014, there are no hostages held in Gaza.  The Hostages and Missing Families Forum was established one day after October 7, with a single, urgent mission: to bring home the 255 men, women, and children taken hostage to Gaza. What began as a moment of unimaginable shock became one of the most determined civic, moral, and human struggles in history.  Today, 843 days later, that mission has been completed. All 255 hostages have been returned to Israel. 46 of them were abducted alive and murdered in captivity. With the return of Rani Gvili, a hero who gave his life defending his community, we can finally say: there are no longer any hostages in Gaza.  This moment belongs not only to the families, but to the millions in Israel and around the world who stood with us. To every government, organization, journalist, and individual who refused to look away, who raised their voices, applied pressure, and believed this mission could be completed, we offer our deepest gratitude.  The struggle to bring the hostages home has ended 🎗️  Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

text: "To be a free nation in our land" is not just a line in the Israeli anthem “HaTikva” (meaning - The Hope), it is a promise.   Yesterday, at the end of the last Shabbat service in Hostages Square, captivity survivors, families of hostages who came home for rehabilitation and families of hostages who were returned for burial, members of the kibbutz movement and citizens from all over Israel stood side by side, and together we sang "HaTikva."   We sang with faith, love, and pain. We promised ourselves to do everything in our power to be worthy of all those who fell for our country and its people. author: BringThemHomeNow
text: "Shabbat has passed and another one and another one and we are still waiting and we are tired. I see my mother who looks strong but she has a hole in her heart the size of Rani. My hero and strong father is torn every time. Each time a new destination is marked and each time he passes. And we wait."  Shira Goili, Rani's sister, told today in the Kidnapped Square about the pain and hardship that has accompanied her family for 840 days: "What else needs to happen for the actions to be done and the talk to stop? How much longer will we wait as a family, as a country, until those who came out to save are returned? I am proud of my brother, I am angry, but proud. I miss Rani, my brother, my friend, the laughs, the nonsense, the moments The little ones. I miss the way he used to fill the room with his broad shoulders, I miss the way he used to insist that we all be at home until he returns. Thank you for bringing the Shabbat to my family.  Photo Credit: Uriel Ibn Sapir

author: BringThemHomeNow
text: After nearly 28 months of tireless efforts, and as this page now ceases its 24/7 activity, we want to say thank you, from the deepest place in our heart.  To every person who stood by the families, who refused to look away, who stayed. Everyone who took part in this fight to bring the hostages home became part of history, the largest civil movement in Israel since 1948.  You echoed the families’ pain, their cries, and even their rare moments of joy. You embraced the hostages and their families as if we were your family, too. You carried them when they could not carry themselves.  Your likes. Your comments. Your follows. Your shares.  They were never small gestures. Know this: they were a lifeline. They were a wave of human compassion that pierced through the darkest nightmare.  They were threads in a monumental force that moved mountains, touched every corner of the earth, and brought our loved ones home.  One day, when people ask, ‘Where were you during this time?’ You’ll be able to say: I was there. I did not stay silent. I was part of Bring Them Home Now. I helped bring them home.  Thank you for carrying us. Thank you for never giving up. Thank you for bringing them home 💛  Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

author: BringThemHomeNow
text: "Ran Goyili is not just a name, Ran is a son, a friend, a brave YSM fighter who on October 7 ran into the fire and defended with his body Kibbutz Alumim and the home of all of us. Ran fought like a hero and was kidnapped to Gaza. He is a symbol of supreme sacrifice, and thanks to him many of us are alive today." Hadassah, the sister of the late Shlomo Mansour, asked today at the Shabbat reception at the Kidnapped Square to connect two stories of heroism and death that were intertwined in one destiny: "Ran's relationship with us goes back one generation: Itzik, Ran's father, was in the Nahal nucleus in Kibbutz Kissuf, with my beloved brother, Shlomo Mansour. There, among the fields of the Negev, the two met. Itzik talks about Shlomo with praise and appreciation and with great respect, about a good, honest man, one who was always there for others.  My brother, Shlomo Mansour, was brutally kidnapped from his home in Kibbutz Kissuf on October 7 when he was 85 years old and taken handcuffed to his car and from there to Gaza. Those who knew Shlomo know that it is impossible to miss him - with the eternal smile, the light that radiated from him and the famous mustache that was his hallmark. After 513 long and tormented days Solomon was returned to us in a transaction and buried in the land of Kissuf.  The connection between Ran the warrior and Shlomo, the brother and guide, is the story of the beautiful and painful Land of Israel. This is a story about generations of builders and defenders who tied their fate in this land.  Ran continued the same line of values, the same commitment, the same silent statement "if needed, I'm here", and today we should be here for him.  And when we accept Shabbat, we will remember the strength of his spirit, his smile and the light of Ran and the shining smile of Shlomo.  Their light will continue to light our way." Photo credit: Paulina Fatimer, Uriel Ibn Sapir #ישראלמחקהלרני #אדהחטופהאקרון Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

author: BringThemHomeNow
text: The story of the family headquarters for the return of the abducted and missing - the health system and the resilience team The health system worked continuously and intensively from the beginning of the war until the return of the last abductee, while providing comprehensive health care for the families of the abductees, the returnees and all the activities of the headquarters.  The organization developed a multidisciplinary professional doctrine in the field of "health of abductees and families of abductees", published reports and articles and made accessible the health, medical and mental implications of abduction to decision makers in Israel and around the world, with an emphasis on humanitarian and international organizations.  At the same time, a unique professional and public language was formulated to understand the multidimensional damage of the kidnapping and to sharpen the sense of urgency to return all the abductees, alive and dead.   The organization regularly accompanied the families, initiated collaborations with the health system and treatment providers, motivated the health and scientific community in Israel and the world, and took part in professional initiatives, conferences and public activities. In addition to this, he identified and mapped the unique needs of the families of the abductees and the survivors of the captivity, worked for professional advocacy and the exploitation of rights, and accompanied rehabilitation and long-term support, while laying the foundation for future research on the effects of the abduction on the health of the families and the returnees.  The resilience team was established immediately with the establishment of the headquarters, when about ten women and therapists were stationed to help. First the resilience team members joined all the intense protest activities, marches, rallies, demonstrations, and provided emotional support as needed. The caregivers were in close contact with most of the families and their door was open to help anyone who needed it at any hour of the day.  As the struggle dragged on and the headquarters was organized, mental support gradually became structured: a clinic was opened for urgent and short interventions and diagnosis. The clinic has created a significant therapeutic sequence with external therapists for long-term treatments.  In addition, the headquarters teams who worked closely with the families with a huge emotional investment, and especially the family teams, the media teams, the family room team and the field headquarters, received a therapist who joined the teams for counseling, training, and individual help.   As the struggle continued and its consequences on the mental state of the family members, diverse activities were added: group therapy for homogeneous groups, such as families of martyrs, mothers of abductees, young people, etc.; days of respite; Retreats for homogenous groups with two-three days of therapeutic activity and consolidation and relaxatio

author: BringThemHomeNow
text: The story of the headquarters of the families for the return of the kidnapped and the missing - social department The social team has been active since the establishment of the headquarters and led the assimilation of the call Bring Them Home Now, which became the name of the pages and the hashtag associated with the struggle of the families of the abductees.   The team established and operated pages in Hebrew and English on all social networks: Facebook, Instagram, X, Tiktok, LinkedIn and YouTube, and spread the voice of the families of the abductees through original content, interviews, live broadcasts, parades and rallies in Israel and around the world. The headquarters pages on the international platforms reached almost a million followers and in Israeli about half a million, with tens of millions of views per month. Videos uploaded by the headquarters received millions of views in Israel and around the world, and at the peak - over 200 million monthly views on Instagram alone.  The international activity reached followers from Europe to the USA, Australia and the Far East. A uniform and identifiable visual language was developed, which made it possible to identify the headquarters' contents on any platform and in any language.  The team led activities in front of influencers in Israel and around the world. Together, millions of people were exposed to the contents of the headquarters, shared the stories of the abductees and assisted in a joint and strong call for their return.  During the 843 days of the struggle for the return of the abductees, over 50 volunteers took part in the team's activities, which led to unprecedented achievements and the presence of the abductees everywhere and at all times. text: "On October 7, our clock stopped but did not stop running. Rani went out, fought, rescued, was kidnapped and returned and now we can really stop for a moment" Shira, the sister of Israel's hero Major Ran Gueli, the last abductee who was resettled last night, arrived today at the Kidnapped Square for the ceremony of stopping the clock, before her family will bring Rani to eternal rest tomorrow: "For the past 844 days, I have felt every minute, every fraction of a second with longing And waiting for Rani. The world continued to move but I wanted it to stop together with us, on the one hand that the nights would end and on the other that the morning wouldn't come if Rani didn't come back. And now he is here. He and 86 other martyrs were returned to Israel for burial and he is the last.  It's a special place, this square, this square, these are the people, these are you. The families of the abductees who welcomed me with a warm embrace, the employees and volunteers of the family headquarters who set our Rani as a goal and did not give up, and did and gave as they promised until the last abductee included.  Thank you to the people of Israel, to the Diaspora Jews who supported in every possible way. We lost citizens, soldiers and policemen, brave people who went out to protect and save and fight against the evil that surrounds us, you will forever be intertwined in the story of our lives. Thanks to those who are still engaged in fighting, guarding and saving.  We all need to find a way to heal with a big hole in our hearts but a great love for our people and country." text: The story of the headquarters of the families for the return of the kidnapped and missing - spokespeople and international media The international department led one of the largest and most significant international moves in the history of the State of Israel. The department included hundreds of employees and volunteers with field headquarters in 50 countries.  The international media team led unprecedented media coverage: tens of thousands of interviews, hundreds of thousands of articles and quotes that reached hundreds of millions of views. All this while responding to hundreds of international media, organizing tours of the disaster areas, press conferences and collaborations with leading media in English and a variety of other languages. The press releases of the headquarters received a worldwide resonance under the official name "Headquarters of the Families of the Kidnapped and Missing", and the issue was kept at the top of the global public agenda.  In cooperation with the headquarters of the families in the USA, the dozens of delegations that reached the White House, Congress and the Senate were covered by the media, something that strengthened the commitment of the American government to return all the abductees, the living and the dead, and changed the public discourse. author: BringThemHomeNow
text: The Hostages and Missing Families Forum was established on October 8, 2023, less than 24 hours after the devastating attack of October 7th. The Forum, a nonprofit organization founded by hostage families, set itself the goal of bringing home all hostages, regardless of religion, race, or gender. On day 843 of the war, the Forum completed its mission with the return of the last hostage.  Thousands of volunteers joined the Forum, including senior figures from the security, legal, media, health, and diplomatic sectors. Working closely with government ministries, the IDF, foreign governments, and hundreds of communities worldwide, they mobilized rapidly under extreme wartime conditions to achieve unprecedented results. The Forum operates around the clock with two core divisions. The advocacy division leads strategic communications, diplomacy, grassroots organizing, business engagement, and creative campaigns at both Israeli and international levels. The family services division provides logistical, medical, and emotional support while coordinating legal counsel, medical documentation, and family advocacy activities.  💛Farewell💛  The Hostages Forum was established to bring the hostages home and closed upon full completion of its mission with the return of the last hostage. The Forum succeeded in the sacred, values-driven, and moral mission it set for itself: returning 255 of our brothers and sisters from Hamas captivity, some to rehabilitation, some for burial, thanks to the support and involvement of the people of Israel, world Jewry, countless individuals around the world, and assistance from the business sector. Special thanks to the tens of thousands of volunteers and activists in Israel and worldwide.  The effort to keep the hostage issue in public consciousness could not have succeeded without the mobilization of media outlets and journalists who understood the magnitude of the moment and the mission, working day after day, each in their own way, to amplify the voices of those silenced in Hamas tunnels. Even on the most difficult days, they persevered and carried the burden of the mission shoulder to shoulder with us. We thank them for their fruitful, values-driven, and successful cooperation, even when fraught with challenges.  We will forever mourn the destruction and loss inflicted upon us by our enemies and eternally grieve the loss of 46 hostages who could have returned to us alive. We mourn all 87 deceased hostages together with hundreds of our fallen civilians and soldiers, and we extend eternal gratitude to their families for their sacrifice. We send wishes for complete healing to soldiers wounded in body and soul and embrace them with all our hearts.  Day 843, the day the last hostage returned, was the first day since 2014 on which there were no hostages in Gaza. May there never be again, not in Gaza, not anywhere. author: BringThemHomeNow
text: The story of the family headquarters for the return of the abducted and the missing - field headquarters in Israel and around the world hundreds of field headquarters were established in Israel and around the world. Good people who initiated, led and promoted activities for the return of the abductees all over the country and in many other countries as well. Each headquarters has a character and color adapted to the community and the families of the abductees from the area.   The activists led diverse activities: from daily identification shifts at intersections, weekly rallies, fundraising stands and making the issue of the abductees and the struggle accessible to the local community. Initiate collaborations with the local government, the education system, youth movements, local businesses and paint the country yellow. The thousands of volunteers all over the country and the world made sure that at every event and conference the subject of the abductees was mentioned and the fight for their return continued.  Many initiatives were started in the field headquarters such as the yellow shirt in schools on September 1, operation of national convoys and flagging and signage throughout the country.  The operatives and activities of the field headquarters operated on a full volunteer basis, day and night and on Saturdays and holidays, until the return of the last abductee. author: BringThemHomeNow
text: For the first time since 2014, it can be declared that there are no Israeli abductees in Gaza!  The headquarters of the families for the return of the abductees was established the day after the seven in October in order to coordinate all the actions and the struggle for the return of the 255 abductees in Gaza.   Last night an appreciation evening was held for the employees and volunteers of the headquarters since its establishment.  The struggle for the return of the abductees was the most civil, value and moral struggle and millions of Israelis and Diaspora Jews took part in it.   Now 843 days into the war it can be declared that there have been no Israeli abductees in Gaza since 2014. 255 abductees were returned to Israel, of which 46 were abducted alive and murdered in captivity.   Now, when Sharni Goili 'protector of the unknown' and the hero of Israel has returned home, more than two years of struggle can be summed up.  Fight to the last bit 🎗️ Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

author: BringThemHomeNow
text: Thank you @SEPeaceMissions  Without @POTUS and his administration, the hostages would never have come home.  Yesterday was a historic day.  The last remaining hostage in Gaza, Officer Ran Gvili, has been returned home to his family in Israel. He went out on October 7 to save lives, and yesterday he returned to rest in peace in Israel.  Now, ALL 20 living hostages and all 28 deceased hostages in Gaza have now been returned to their families – a monumental, historic feat that few thought was possible. It’s thanks to the hard work of so many, but especially @POTUS, who works tirelessly for peace.   This closes a painful chapter for many, and paves the way for a new future that can be defined by peace, not war, and prosperity, not destruction.  It’s a new day in the Middle East, and President Trump, myself, and the entire team are committed to sustained peace and prosperity for all in the region. - Special Envoy Steve Witkoff  Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

text: The Gueli family appeals to the security cabinet ministers ahead of the meeting tonight: "Don't give in to Hamas terror! Please, we appeal to you as a mother and father and as citizens of the State of Israel, whose safety and the safety of its citizens stood before Rani's eyes when he put on a uniform and went out to save lives that terrible morning: do not forget him, do not skip over him, do not leave him behind and do not agree to the opening of the Rafah crossing before Rani is home. author: BringThemHomeNow
text: Exactly one year ago Ofer Kalderon, Yarden Bibas, and Keith Siegel crossed the border and returned home. Through tears, we watched them fall into the arms of their loved ones.   Since then, we’ve watched them begin to piece their lives back together, bravely sharing some of the ordeals they endured in the hell of Gaza.  Almost immediately, they joined the fight to bring the rest home, until the last hostage.  Their strength and courage helped unite the Israeli people and supporters around the world.  Now that there are no hostages left in Gaza, our work continues. We must help them heal. We must help all the families heal. We must help our people heal. author: BringThemHomeNow
text: “For 844 days, the clock kept running, counting every day, every minute, every second since our world stopped on October 7th. We never imagined that clock would reach three digits, and we feared it would reach four. Thank God we can finally stop counting.”  Malki Shem Tov was very emotional at Hostages Square today. His son Omer came home after 505 days in captivity, but their family couldn’t begin to heal as long as there were still hostages in Gaza. Today, when the last hostage is returned, he could stop counting days and finally thank all the people who stood by the families:  “To the people around the world, across every nation, who stood by our families from day one, who made sure we were heard, who ensured our loved ones were never forgotten, we are forever grateful.  Thank you, President Trump, Ambassador Witkoff, Jared Kushner, and the entire U.S. administration for making this day possible.  All the hostages have come home, but this is not a victory. 46 were taken alive and murdered in captivity. We must never forget what happened on October 7th and the more than two years that followed.  This is a day we hoped for, but we carry the weight of what was lost, and we must never forget.”  Photo credit: Lior Rothstein, Hagit Halperin  Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

author: BringThemHomeNow
text: Last night, we witnessed a love story stronger than life itself. Arbel Yehoud and Ariel Cunio spoke of captivity, from the horror of October 7th, when they were torn apart with cruelty, to the fragile attempt now to gather what remains and begin again.  With rare courage, Arbel opened a small crack into her personal hell, the one we feared most. She broke our hearts and left no eye dry as she shared that she endured sexual abuse throughout her captivity, yet still cannot fully speak of it, keeping the pain sealed tightly inside a closed “suitcase.”  And still, despite the shattering pain, we must look Arbel in the eyes. Listen. Believe. Carry her words into the world. And hold her, and Ariel, close from afar.  This love must prevail ❤️‍🩹  Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

author: BringThemHomeNow
text: Today, with the ascension of the family of the late Rani Goili to the grave at the end of the seven days, one of the most terrible and painful periods the people of Israel have known ends. The family, friends, comrades-in-arms and Israeli police officers and many others gathered this morning at the fresh grave of Rani Goili, a hero of Israel and defender of the unknown.   Rani, the last remaining abductee in Gaza, was finally laid to rest - not as we had hoped, but as it had to happen: at home, on his land, surrounded by the love of his family and people.  This is a moment of deep mourning, but also of closing a painful national circle. 255 abductees were returned to Israel. 87 were placed as victims, each one a world and full, each of them an open wound in the hearts of the families and in the heart of the entire country.  The headquarters of the families for the return of the abductees ends its activity with a sense of unrelenting pain for all those who could be with us here today and are not, but also with a clear knowledge: the struggle was waged in the name of the values ​​of the State of Israel and the people of Israel. The values ​​of mutual guarantee, social solidarity and the duty to return home every abductee regardless of religion, race and gender, soldiers and civilians, living or dead.   This historic struggle for their return will be engraved in the national memory as a reminder of the unimaginable human cost of October 7, and of the deep commitment of Israeli society to the families, the missing and the missing. It was also the beautiful hour of the people of Israel who took to the streets en masse, all over the country in the name of these values.  On this day, we will also cherish the soldiers and women of the IDF and all the security forces for a very long and bloody fight. We will send a blessing of recovery to all those wounded in body and soul and we will forever be grateful to all the bereaved families who lost the most precious to them of all. We bow our heads to the Goyili family and to all the families of the martyrs, and pray that we will never have to fight like this again. This is the time for restoration, for all the people of Israel. Photography: Uriel Ibn Sapir Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

text: Tonight, the last rally of the Kibbutz Nir Oz community was held in the Gat vineyards. Kibbutz Nir Oz suffered the heaviest blow on October 7 when one out of four members of the kibbutz was murdered or kidnapped. Only 8 houses in the kibbutz remained undamaged. Since then, every Shabbat, the community has allowed the families of the abductees and members of the community to participate in a more intimate gathering, closer to their temporary home. author: BringThemHomeNow
text: The story of the headquarters of the families for the return of the kidnapped and missing persons - the abductees' square The headquarters began its activity in the museum tower, and later moved to the Check Point building, which hosted the headquarters until its closure. The Museum Square, courtesy of the Tel Aviv Municipality, was converted into the Kidnapped Square and became, next to the Ariela House, the central space of the headquarters and the families.  The square was a second home for the members of the families, a focal point for rallies, press conferences, exhibitions and events, and a place of pilgrimage for supporters of the struggle from Israel and the world.  The square was also the beating heart of the struggle and the direct connection with the public, who came to it for thousands of events - rallies, Shabbat receptions, birthdays, prayers and statements to the media and was a space of support, reinforcement and mutual guarantee. This is also the place where the Israeli and international media operated, alongside ongoing activities and trainings for volunteer teams.  In the nearby Ariela house, the "Family Room" was established - a quiet, protected and intimate space, where dozens of volunteers provided hot food, activities for children and a meeting place for the families, allowing them to be together, strengthen and feel at home.  Photographs: 24.10.23 - at the announcement of the Kidnapped Square (credit Eyal Radoshinsky) 24.10.23 - the establishment of the square (credit Roni Shapira) Gilad Korngold, Tal Shoham's father in training at the Kidnapped Square (credit Mata Hatofim) Unfurling the huge flag just before the start of the rally to mark the 600th day in the square (credit Mata Hamalim Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

author: BringThemHomeNow
text: The story of the families headquarters for the return of the abducted and missing - the family team The family team was the beating heart of the families, a source of warmth, comfort and unconditional love. The team connected the families with the professionals, maintained direct and daily contact with them and constituted a central address for the families for any need.  The team leaders accompanied, coordinated and supported the families while responding to their needs, coordinated between parties at the headquarters and outside, assisted in the preparation for formal and informal meetings, delegations abroad for leaders and government officials in Israel and around the world.  The families know how to tell about the endless support and generosity of the team members. They were a reason and an incentive to get up in the morning even on dark days. With their help, the helplessness of many families turned into a sense of ability, despair into hope and sorrow and loneliness into companionship and comfort.   The families' team included a complete escort system consisting of dozens of volunteers who formed the backbone of the work and support for the families.  The team of counselors worked day and night to help families in every possible field while providing a continuous response and a broad view of the needs, all out of a deep commitment and uncompromising human responsibility.  The attendants, in cooperation with the family team, connected the family members with the various staff members, helped and cared for the family members in all areas of life, starting with logistical and bureaucratic needs and ending with emotional support and assistance in their struggle to return their loved ones. In this way, it was possible for the families to maintain both their dignity and their unique voice, and also to place it at the center of the public struggle for the return of their loved ones in Israel and around the world.  The attendants have become members of the family's household, with many of them staying in touch even with the return of their loved ones, and some accompanying the survivors to this day.  Photo credit: families team 02.2024 - The families march from Raim parking lot to Jerusalem. 04.2024 - Passover "Hag" dinner for families at Beit Ariela in Hatofim square. Conversation circles led by families and with the participation of the public in the Kidnapped Square. Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

author: BringThemHomeNow
text: One year since the deal that brought home 33 Israeli hostages alongside 5 Thai hostages.  Mothers of returned hostages stood beside Talik Gvili and joined her call: “A mother never gives up.”  Together, they dedicated this call to Ran Gvili, the last hostage still in Gaza.  “We promised, until the last hostage. Ran is now the son of all of us. As a mother, I share Talik’s pain that Ran is the last one in captivity” said Niva, mother of captivity survivor Omer Wenkert.  These mothers know exactly what Talik is living through. And they continue to stand with her, raising a mother’s cry for her son’s return. author: BringThemHomeNow
text: Today, after receiving the Shabbat for Rani's return, which takes place every week in Hatofim Square, the Chief of Staff stopped his car outside the Kariya base and spoke with Tlik and Itzik, the parents of Major Ran Goili.   The Chief of Staff insisted on the IDF's commitment to return Rani home and emphasized that the task of repatriating him is a task that is in the minds and hearts of all IDF soldiers, from the Chief of Staff to the last of the soldiers.  The Chief of Staff also added that the IDF and the Southern Command are working all the time in all efforts to bring him home as soon as possible.   Shelly Rani's parents thanked the Chief of Staff for his commitment to bring Rani back and told him they trusted him. text: "At night I wait to see your face again with closed eyes. Come in my dreams, send me signs" Yesterday, the family of Sgt. His is in the youth movement of the Mashchim, and on it is the inscription "Kif and half to me", a kind of inside joke of his and theirs because he did not like to "waste" time on clapping, and therefore instituted an amusing practice of clapping his hands briefly.   "We created a powerful and touching song together, I couldn't imagine that they would understand me like that. It helps me deal with Itay's birthday" said Hagit. "When I heard the song, I felt that my voice should be heard as well. I'm not a singer and I've never sung, but I mustered up my strength and courage and went with Ruby, Itay's father, to Kibbutz Dalia to the studio of Eran, Amri's partner who produced the song, and we added the last chorus in my voice." text: מטה המשפחות להחזרת החטופים והנעדרים הוקם פחות מיממה אחרי המתקפה ההרסנית של החמאס על ערים, קיבוצים, ישובים, בסיסי צה״ל ומשתתפי פסטיבל הנובה ב-7 באוקטובר 2023. משימתו של המטה, שנוסד על ידי בני משפחות החטופים הישראלים, היתה לפעול בכל הערוצים האפשריים, בארץ ובעולם, כדי להחזיר את יקיריהם הביתה, בכל דרך ובמהירות האפשרית. מטרת ההתארגנות האזרחית תחילה הייתה התאגדות המשפחות אך מהר מאוד הובן כי המטה יהיה מטה מאבק ובה בעת, בית לתמיכה בבני משפחות החטופים. המטה העניק מענים למשפחות בכל תחום אפשרי: אישי, רפואי, משפטי, חוסן ובית. זאת הרבה לפני שהמדינה התעשתה והייתה שם למענם. המטה הפך את המשפחות לקהילה ויצר עבורם בית ומקלט לשהות בו בימים האפלים של חייהם.  במטה שהוביל את המאבק האזרחי המוסרי והערכי ביותר בהיסטוריה של מדינת ישראל, התנדבו אלפי א.נשים ביניהם דמויות בכירות מהמגזר הביטחוני, המשפטי, התקשורתי, בריאותי והדיפלומטי בשיתוף פעולה הדוק עם משרדי ממשלה, צה"ל, ממשלות זרות ומאות קהילות ברחבי העולם. זו הייתה התארגנות מהירה, תחת תנאי מלחמה ובסיטואציה שאינה מוכרת לאף אחד מאנשי המקצוע שלקחו חלק בהקמתו ובניהולו.  על אף הקשיים, המטה הגיע להישגים בכל התחומים, כאלה שלא נראו כמותם בשום גוף אחר בארץ או בעולם. כדי לשמר את המאבק לאורך הזמן הנדרש, כארבעה חודשים לאחר הקמתו, העמותה החלה להעסיק עשרות עובדים מתוך מאות המתנדבים שישמשו גרעין קבוע והכרחי לעבודת המטה באופן רציף ויעיל.  המטה פעל 24 שעות ביממה, 7 ימים בשבוע כדי לסייע לבני המשפחות בכל צרכיהן, זאת כאשר לא היה מענה וסיוע ממקור אחר. 'קומת המאבק' במטה הובילה את הפן האסטרטגי, תקשורתי (ישראלי ובינ"ל), דיפלומטי, שטח, מגזר עסקי, פרסום וקראייטיב, יועצים מגזריים ועוד. 'קומת המשפחות' סייעה למשפחות לוגיסטית, רפואית, חוסן ועוד במטרה לאפשר לבני המשפחות להתמודד עם הכאב והלחץ ולהתמקד במאבק. בקומה זו היו מחלקות נוספות לתמיכה וסיוע במאבק - ייעוץ משפטי ישראלי ובינלאומי, דוחות ומחקרים רפואיים וריכוז פעילות בני המשפחות במאבק.  💛מילות פרידה 💛  מטה החטופים הוקם כדי להחזיר את החטופים ונסגר עם השלמת המשימה במלואה- החזרתו של החטוף האחרון. המטה הצליח במשימה הקדושה, הערכית והמוסרית שהציב לעצמו והיא השבת 255 אחינו ואחיותינו משבי החמאס, מי לשיקום ומי למנוחת עולמים בזכות התמיכה והמעורבות של עם ישראל, יהודי העולם בתפוצות והסיוע מן המגזר העסקי. תודה מיוחדת גם לעשרות אלפי המתנדבים והמתנדבות, הפעילים והפעילות בארץ ובעולם, אתם ישראל היפה!  המאמץ להשארת נושא החטופים בתודעה הציבורית לא יכול היה להצליח ללא הירתמותם של כלי התקשורת וחבורת עיתונאים ועיתונאיות שהבינו את גודל השעה והמשימה, ודאגו יום אחר יום, כל אחד בדרכו, להשמיע את קולם של אלו שקולם נאלם במנהרות החמאס. גם בימים המורכבים ביותר, הם לא ויתרו ונשאו איתנו כתף אל כתף את נטל המשימה. אנו מודים להם על שיתוף פעולה פורה, ערכי ומוצלח, גם אם היה רווי אתגרים מעת לעת.  לעד נכאב את ההרס והאובדן שהסבו עלינו אויבנו ולנצח נבכה על אובדן 46 החטופים שיכלו לחזור אלינו בחיים. נתאבל על כל 87 החטופים החללים ביחד עם מאות אחינו ואחיותינו חללי המלחמה ונוקיר תודת עולמים למשפחותיהם על קורבנם. נשלח מפה ברכת רפואה שלמה לפצועי צה"ל בגוף ובנפש ונחבק אותם בכל ליבנו.  היום ה- 843, יום השבתו של החטוף האחרון, היה היום הראשון מאז שנת 2014 שבו לא היו חטופים ישראלים בעזה, והלוואי ולא יהיו עוד לעולם, לא בעזה ולא בכלל. אבל אם חלילה יהיו, תדע

author: BringThemHomeNow
text: Today Itai Sbirsky should have celebrated his 41st birthday, but he will forever remain 38. Itai was born in Bari on February 17, 1985, third child to Rafi and Orit, brother to Merev and Yonatan, and later also to Yuval.  With me was a curious and sensitive boy, with golden curls and a shy half smile.  Already in his childhood photos, you can see his kind eyes and the inquisitive look, sensitive to the environment. A gifted athlete, starting with Barry's basketball team, through tennis lessons and ending with soccer. His classmates in the "Apple" class say that he was one level above everyone else. Itay was also a die-hard fan of Maccabi Tel Aviv. In his youth, his love for music developed. He studied voice development and enjoyed playing the guitar and piano.  Itay served in the air traffic control unit (IA). After his release and the trip to India, he moved to Tel Aviv and began studying at the university. Along with his studies, he continued personal development processes and fell in love with Brazilian jiu-jitsu, which became an integral part of his life. From a young age, Itay dealt with philosophical questions, with curiosity and a willingness to listen to the other side and learn new things. This is how he came to the Satya method; first as a trainee and later as a trainer himself. Friends and family They say that the method allowed him to express his wonderful ability to listen deeply to what he heard. He was the perfect uncle to his parents and a grandson who made sure to visit his grandmother as much as possible. On Friday, October 6th, the brutal attack on the kibbutz caught him At his mother Orit's. They both locked themselves in the MMD, with gunshots and shouts in Arabic all around them. The family members kept in touch through the joint WhatsApp group. Slowly and gradually the ties were severed: first with Rafi, then with Itai, and last was Orit. She sent a heart, and another heart.  Orit and Rafi were murdered in Bari on October 7. Itay was kidnapped alive. On the 97th day of his captivity, the building where he was held, along with Noa Argamani and the late Yossi Sharabi, collapsed on them. Itay survived and managed to rescue himself. Days later, after 99 days in captivity in Gaza, he was murdered by his captors. With the release of Noa Argamani, who was with Itay in captivity until his last moments, we learned that even in the inhumane conditions in which they were held, Itay remained who he was: he showed resourcefulness and recruited the All his powers and abilities to survive under constant threat, and he had the courage to be there for others as well. Today, let's stop for a moment and remember him, a man of connection and humanity. Open, curious, and always looking to see others. In his memory 💔 Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

author: BringThemHomeNow
text: "In the Torah we have a very clear commandment - 'You shall not stand on the blood of your neighbor.' This is the basis for the value of evils, for the mutual guarantee, that no one is left behind. A value anchored in the spirit of the IDF."  Deborah, the mother of the late Tzachi Idan, who was kidnapped alive, murdered in captivity and returned for burial about a year ago, was one of the Shabbat acceptance initiatives in the square.  Today she came to speak in front of families of abductees, survivors of captivity, members of the kibbutzim movement and the large crowd, the last time we accept Shabbat together: "Today, we are 847 days since the terrible disaster of October 7th. After 510 days of uncertainty, with terrible pain, we accepted Tzachi as a space.  This pain has become a part of our lives, something that lives within us every day anew.  Today I am here to thank you from the bottom of my heart for all the moments that you were hope for us. Thank you for the strength and support we received from the kibbutz movement from the Nahal Oz community for generations from you here, from our people.    The pain is heavy, but the hope is also great. With this hope, I believe we are committed to act, strengthen and build.   Despite all the disputes, anger and hatred, there is one value that unites us, a value we all know, and that is "love your neighbor as yourself".  This is not just a verse from the Torah, it is a sentence that binds and sustains our society.    And today our responsibility is clear: to act with determination, to maintain unity, respect and love even when we are different. It is a duty, not just a right. For all those who are not with us, for the correction, for a better future for our children. Because that's the only way we'll build a strong, good and united society that we can all be excited about and proud of." Photo credit: Alon Gilboa Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

This is a family, we are all a family. It's not 'together we will win,' together is the victory! My brother Keith and my sister-in-law Aviva were kidnapped Aviva was in captivity for 484 days. 46 abductees were killed in captivity.
