text: Ran Gueli, the last abductee, was returned home after 843 days 💔 Colonel Ran Gueli, a YSM fighter, fell in the battle defending Kibbutz Alumim on October 7. 24 years old in Naples.  Major Ran (Rani) Goili from Mitar was a Negev YSM fighter in the southern district. Ren was proud to be a policeman and to wear the blue uniform.  On the morning of Black Sabbath, Rani was injured at home with a fractured shoulder following a motorcycle accident, but as soon as he heard about the terrorists' infiltration, he put on a uniform and went out to help his friends from the unit in fighting. On the way he encountered terrorists and fought fiercely and ferociously at the front of the battle at the entrance to Kibbutz Alumim, and even received the nickname "Ran Magen Alumim" from the Kibbutz community.   After several months, an assessment was received that after a stubborn battle and only after he ran out of ammunition, Ran fell in battle and was kidnapped to Gaza.   Ran with the big smile and broad shoulders was all about a huge heart, a true friend, loved by everyone, loved to enjoy life, a young and noble man, always spoke at the level of the poor with a powerful and peaceful presence.  Ran is survived by his parents Itzik and Tilik, his brother Omri and his sister Shira.  The headquarters of the families of the abductees mourns and bows their heads in memory of Ran and participates in the deep sorrow of the Goyili family.  The last abductee, Ran Goili, returned home 🎗️ Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

author: BringThemHomeNow
text: Ran Gvili, the last hostage, is brought home after 843 days 💔  First to enter. Last to return.  Staff Sergeant Ran (Rani) Gvili from Meitar was a YASSAM Negev fighter in the Southern District of the Israel Police. Ran took great pride in being a police officer and wearing the blue uniform.  On the morning of October 7th, Ran was at home recovering from a motorcycle accident and suffering from a fractured shoulder. Upon learning of the terrorist infiltration, he immediately put on his uniform and went out to assist his fellow unit members in the fighting. On his way, he encountered terrorists and fought with courage and determination on the front line at the entrance to Kibbutz Alumim. Members of the kibbutz community later gave him the name “Ran, the Defender of Alumim.”  After several months, assessments concluded that following a fierce battle, and only after his ammunition had run out, Ran fell in combat and was abducted to Gaza.  Ran, with his broad shoulders and radiant smile, was all heart. A true friend, loved by everyone. He loved life, was a young man of deep values, always spoke at eye level, and carried a powerful yet calm presence. At 24 years old at the time of his death, Ran is survived by his parents, Talik and Itzik, his brother Omri, his sister Shira, and an extended family.  Ran Gvili was the last hostage 🎗️  The Hostages and Missing Families Forum bows its head in sorrow and shares in the profound grief of the Gvili family.  There are no words to express the depth of this pain.  Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

author: BringThemHomeNow
text: Clock Stopping Ceremony at Hostages Square  📌Tuesday | January 27 | 5:30 PM | Hostages Square, Tel Aviv  The iconic Hostages Square was home to the families of the hostages and the heart of the Hostages and Missing Families Forum, a gathering place for countless Israelis and people from around the world who came to support the families and stand with them throughout the struggle. One of the square’s most powerful symbols was the stopwatch, counting the days, minutes, and seconds that our loved ones were held captive by Hamas.  The clock became an inseparable part of the square, always present and visible at rallies, moments of hope, and moments of deep pain.  Now, following the return of the last hostage, Ran Gvili, an Israeli hero, the time has finally come to stop the clock.  Join us in reciting the Jewish "Shehecheyanu" blessing of gratitude, recited to thank God for enabling one to reach new, special, often long awaited milestones. Given this knowledge, we urge that pressure be directed where it belongs: on Hamas to fulfill its obligations under the agreement. Hamas is deceiving the international community and refusing to return our son, the last remaining hostage, in what constitutes a clear violation of the agreement it signed.  We ask that the Prime Minister of Israel make clear to the respected American envoys that anyone who truly seeks to advance the rehabilitation of Gaza and peace in the Middle East must first and foremost bring Rani home." author: BringThemHomeNow
text: Today Alex Lubanov should have celebrated his 35th birthday, but forever he will remain 33 years old. Alexander (Alex) Lubanov, was born on 18.02.1991 in Russia. When he was 8 years old, he immigrated to Israel with his family. Alex fit in wonderfully at school, was a sociable, self-confident and ambitious child. He always set goals for himself and enjoyed achieving them. His love for the kitchen led him to work after his military service as a cook at the Fishenzon restaurant in the marina in Ashkelon, where in 2013 he met Michal who worked there as a waitress. Over the years they fell in love and got married. His big dream was to open a restaurant on the beach.  Alex loved to travel very much. He joined the community "Subaru and Jeeps travel for free", and over the years he was among the leaders of the community. With the birth of his eldest son, Tom, in 2021, Alex combined his love for traveling with his love for his son. He would pick him up from kindergarten and they would go on jeep trips together. Alex regularly volunteered at the "Yadidis" organization, which provides first aid on the roads. He greatly assisted the army and the police in rescuing civilians and vehicles His friends and family always knew that he could be trusted in everything. In his spare time, Alex used to spend time with his family and friends. He loved diving, listening to music and cooking. On October 6, 2023, he was in charge of the bar and the bartenders On the morning of October 7, Alex reassured her that they were getting ready to go home. He decided to run away with his friends towards the forest near Kibbutz Bari. At around nine in the morning, his family received the news that Alex had been captured for 11 months Michal had their second son and named him Kai. Michal believed with all her heart that Alex would return home and get to know Kai. After the birth, she also asked to send a message to Alex: "I want to tell you that you have to come back and see how much Kai looks like you, how much Tom is waiting for you. You need to be strong, just as we are strong for you." On August 29, 2024, the terrorists guarding Alex Lubnov, Hersh Goldberg-Polin, Carmel Gat, Uri Danino, Aden Yerushalmi and Almog Sarosi murdered the six abductees in a tunnel in Gaza. Two days later, during an IDF operation in the Tel Sultan neighborhood of Rafah, their bodies were located and returned to Israel.  Alex left behind his wife Michal, his children Tom and Kai, his parents Oksana and Gregory and his brother Anton.   Today, we will stop for a moment and remember Alex. A guy with a big heart, a captivating smile, and a rollicking laugh full of joy. A moral and optimistic guy who loved nature, lived the sea and above all loved to help and contribute to others wholeheartedly.  In his memory 💔 Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

author: BringThemHomeNow
text: Forever young - today Shani Lok should have celebrated her 25th birthday, but she will forever remain 22. Shani was born on February 7, 2001 in Moshav Adrat. Daughter of Nissim and Ricarda (Ricky) who came from Germany and fell in love with Israel and Judaism. Sister to Adi to Amit and Or. At the age of two, she moved to live with her family in the settlement of Serigi.  Shani was a beautiful, creative and independent girl, with a big and compassionate heart. From a young age, her love for art sprouted. Whether music, dance, writing, fashion design, hair design or sewing. In high school she combined theoretical studies alongside art studies. When she matured, she moved to Tel Aviv, where she lived with friends, studied graphic design and worked as a tattoo artist.  Shani's other love was to travel and get to know other languages ​​and cultures. During her travels she participated in many music festivals around the world and in one of them she met Orion Hernandez Rado, a talented music producer from Mexico, who became her partner and even came with her to the Nova festival.   On the morning of October 7, Shani and Orion tried to escape the terror of the missiles. They were traveling in a car with their friend Keshet Kasruti, but unfortunately the terrorists closed in on them. The three friends were murdered and Orion and Shani were kidnapped to Gaza.   Her big dream of setting up a big studio, where she will do tattoos and dreadlocks, and sell clothes designed by her, especially clothes for festivals, she will no longer be able to fulfill.   Riki's mother said: "For dinner on Friday. On October 6, before the terrible day, I told her to come with Orion. We didn't meet him and we really wanted to get to know him. She said that they were going to a party with bad guys and that they wouldn't be enough, but she promised that she would come with him to dinner the following Friday. Who knew, there wouldn't be a next Friday."  Today, let's stop for a moment and we will all remember the beautiful and lively Shani, who loved music and danced through life, until the terrible day when the melody of her life was cruelly stopped. text: "We are at the end of a period, a very long period of madness. Crazy things that we didn't think this nation would go through and lo and behold this period is over. The last of the abductees returned with the help of everyone's mutual guarantee." Shlomo Alfasa, brother-in-law of Mia Goren who was abducted and returned for burial, spoke today at the Shabbat reception in the square about the solidarity that was created between the families of the abductees, alongside the different needs of each family: "During this period each family 'chased' its abductee and together there was solidarity between the families.  In our particular case, Mia was rescued after 292 days and we decided in our heart and soul to be with the other families of the abductees and to continue for 551 days until the last of the abductees returned."  Along with the general struggle for the return of the abductees, the family worked to change the regulation and recognize adult orphans, a process that was led by the families of the abductees with the assistance of the legal department of the headquarters of the families of the abductees and came to an end this week. text: We, the families of the hostages, have been there since October 7, because we had no choice. We had to bring our loved ones home. author: BringThemHomeNow
text: The story of the family headquarters for the return of the abducted and the missing - spokespeople and Israeli media The Israeli communications department was a central axis in the struggle for the return of the abductees and has operated continuously since the establishment of the headquarters. The department led the full media response: formulating and distributing messages to the media, mobilizing public opinion in Israel and around the world, conducting thousands of interviews and articles on all media platforms, preparing and accompanying the families of the abductees to public and media appearances.  The media team led coverage of hundreds of rallies, marches, statements and events for the abductees, day and night, on Saturdays and holidays. The team led special broadcast days, dozens of coverage points at the same time and led coverage like no other in Israel. The subject of the abductees was present in tens of thousands of items and articles on television, radio, written and online press, in podcasts, playlists and in every possible way.  The team led to unprecedented achievements in the scope of media exposure in all its aspects and thanks to them, among other things, the subject of the abductees did not drop from the public agenda from the beginning of the war until the return of the last abductee.  The team provided a professional and available response to the media around the clock, and worked to create a consistent and clear public presence of the abductees issue, while adapting the messages to the moment, the scene and the changing needs of the struggle.  Through the in-depth work of dozens of workers and volunteers, the media served as a significant tool for the presence of the abductees, for connecting the public to the struggle and for leading a responsible, humane and valuable discourse throughout.  Photos: press conference of the families on the seventh day of Iron Swords at the headquarters of the families in the museum tower (credit Nadav Cohen Yonatan). 4.12.23 - press conference calling for an urgent cabinet meeting at the families' headquarters (credit Eyal Radoshinsky) 04.26.2024 - behind the scenes at an interview with four mothers of the observers (credit the families of the abductees) 12.05.2025 - a viewing point at the Alexander family home on the day of Idan Alexander's release (credit Paulina Petimer) Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

author: BringThemHomeNow
text: 845 days after October 7, Major Ran Goili, Magen Alumim, the first to enter and the last to return, is laid to rest. In a ceremony in Mitar in the presence of family members, friends, his unit mates, members of the families of the abductees and in the presence of the Prime Minister, the Commissioner, the Chief Rabbi of Israel, the Ministers of Defense and the Interior, the funeral ceremony was held for Rani Goili, a hero of Israel. Major Ran (Rani) Goili, late of Mitar He was a Negev YSM fighter in the southern district. Ran was proud to be a policeman and to wear the blue uniform. On the morning of Black Shabbat, Ran was injured at home with a fractured shoulder following a motorcycle accident, but as soon as he heard about the terrorists' infiltration, he put on a uniform and went out to help his friends from the unit in fighting. On the way to his friends, he encountered terrorists and acted with strength and ferocity at the front of the battle at the entrance to Kibbutz Alumim, and even received the nickname "Ran Magen Alumim" From the kibbutz community. After a stubborn battle, Ran fell in battle and was taken to Gaza. He was a true friend, loved by everyone, an honest man with principles and values. He was 24 years old and left behind his parents, Tlik and Itzik. His brother Omri, his sister Anifa, was the last abductee. Photo credit: Uriel Ibn Sapir. author: BringThemHomeNow
text: "Three and a half months ago I was in a completely different place, with no one to pick me up in moments of crisis, to laugh or cry with me, just alone." With these words, Ariel Konio opened his words this evening, at the last rally of Carmi Gat.   "Today I stand here together with my brother David, who returned with me from captivity, surrounded by so many amazing people. We both stand here as living proof that even in the face of the most terrible darkness, the human spirit can win." And David added and shared: "There were many nights when I didn't know if I would get to see daylight again, if I would hug my childhood again, if I would get to see them laugh, if I would ever return home. And here I am." David, Ariel and their family members thanked everyone who went out to the streets and squares to call for their release, to those who fought for them in the various sectors and to all those who did not stop, until the last abductee. author: BringThemHomeNow
text: "Rani's family is now at seven, they want to thank everyone who came, and everyone who stayed with them all along the way. The family wants to thank all of you, for the support, for the love, and for making them feel that Rani really is the son of all of us."  Emmanuel (Mano) Ohion, arrived for the last Shabbat reception in the square with Bar and Tom by his side, to thank all those who continued to call for the return of their good friend Rani Goili, the late, even when he was the last abductee: "The kibbutz movement, together with many good people, chose to dedicate the Shabbat receptions to Rani. Be there, remind, don't give up. This is the beautiful and united Israel. It is Israel that mutual guarantee is a candle to its feet.   It's hard to explain in words what we feel. There is relief, there is excitement, there is gratitude and there is also such a deep silence of the end of a long road. We have waited so long for this moment. So many Saturdays we stood here, with hope, with pain, with faith, and sometimes without even knowing how to continue.  Those who know Rani know that he is a person of presence. of heart And just as he knew how to be there for others, so this people knew how to be there for him. The hug we received from all of you, the prayers, the messages, coming here week after week, was strength. real power.  This day is not just the end of an era. He is also a beginning. The beginning of returning home, of healing, of life. And we ask you one thing: take this spirit, this guarantee with you. The memory of what it is to be together.  Because that's what brought Rani home. And that is what will keep us going. Thank you from the bottom of my heart.'  Photo credit: Alon Gilboa, Uriel Ibn Sapir Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

text: Last night we watched a love story stronger than life itself in the Friday studio, when Arbel Yehud and Ariel Kunio told about their entire period of captivity, from the terrible October Seven, when they were brutally torn from each other to their attempt now to pick up the pieces and rebuild their lives.  Brave Arbel opened a crack for us into her hell, the one we feared more than anything. She broke our hearts and didn't leave a single dry eye when she shared that she was attacked and harassed during the entire period of captivity but is still unable to talk about it and keeps it safely in a closed "suitcase".   Despite the crushing pain, we must all look Arbel in the eyes, listen to her, tell the world what she chose to share with courage and hug her and Ariel from afar. author: BringThemHomeNow
text: Ahead of this evening’s Security Cabinet meeting, the Gvili family issues an urgent appeal to Cabinet members:  “Do not surrender to Hamas terror. Moving to Phase Two must first and foremost include the return of all hostages.  Hamas is still holding our son, Ran, captive. Hamas has not disarmed, and the State of Israel cannot proceed with opening the Rafah Crossing while Hamas continues to deceive the world.  We appeal to you as parents and as citizens of the State of Israel. Ran placed the safety of Israel and its people above his own when he put on his uniform and went out to save lives on that terrible morning.  We ask that he not be forgotten, passed over, or left behind. Any steps regarding the opening of the Rafah Crossing should take place only after Ran has returned home.  Israel must not forget its heroes. First and foremost, Ran must be brought home.”  Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

author: BringThemHomeNow
text: Family members, friends, fellow soldiers, Israel Police officers, and many others gathered this morning at the fresh grave of Master Sgt. Ran Gvili, as his family visited his final resting place following the conclusion of the “Shivaa” (the Jewish seven-day mourning period).  This is a moment of profound grief, but also a painful national reckoning. All 255 hostages held in Gaza, including all 251 hostages abducted on October 7 were returned to Israel. 87 were returned deceased - each a world unto themselves, each an open wound in the hearts of their families and of the nation as a whole.  The Hostages and Missing Families Forum is concluding its activities with deep grief for all those who should have been with us today and are not, and with the conviction that the struggle was carried out in the name of Israel’s core values: mutual responsibility, solidarity, and the obligation to bring every hostage home - soldier or civilian, living or deceased.  This historic effort will remain etched in the national memory as a reminder of the price paid on October 7 and of the profound commitment shown by Israeli society.  On this day, we also honor the soldiers of the Israel Defense Forces and all security forces for a long and bloody campaign, extend wishes for healing to all those wounded in body and spirit, and express enduring gratitude to the bereaved families who paid the heaviest price of all.  We bow our heads to the Gvili family and to all families of the fallen, and pray that the people of Israel will never again be forced to endure such a struggle. This is a moment for mourning and for healing for the entire nation.  Photo credit: Uriel Even Sapir  Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

text: "On October 843, 2023, the last abductee was returned home: Ran Gueli, hero of Israel, defender of the unknown, was returned to eternal rest. author: BringThemHomeNow
text: The story of the headquarters of the families for the return of the abducted and the missing - the legal department The legal department has been active since the establishment of the headquarters on a variety of levels, in Israel and in the international arena, to promote the fight for the return of the abductees and to protect their rights and the rights of their families.  The department led the promotion of legislation and policies concerning the rights of abductees, returnees and their families; Worked to raise the issue of the abductees and Hamas crimes in international institutions, led by the UN; and protection of the rights of the abductees and their families as victims of a crime against the state authorities.  As part of its activities in the international arena, the department submitted an official complaint to the International Criminal Court against the leaders of Hamas, demanding justice for war crimes, sexual abuse and abuse of kidnapped children and the children of the kidnapped families, for which international legal recognition was registered. In addition, the legal team initiated senior visits from the UN and the Red Cross to Israel, meetings with the families of the abductees, assisted in the legal battle against UNRWA, and resulted in the conviction of the spreaders of false rumors in the Israeli courts.   Alongside this, the department worked to maintain privacy and medical confidentiality, assisted in the mapping and extraction of rights and ongoing legal support for families, and took care of all the legal aspects required for the operations of the headquarters.  Photographs: 3.12.23 - The visit of the chief prosecutor of the International Criminal Court in The Hague to the headquarters of the families 02.14.24 - Travel of families of abductees and survivors of captivity to file a complaint against Hamas leaders at the International Court in The Hague (credit Eyal Radoshitzky) 01.08.24 - Eilat Samrano stands in front of the UNRA Secretary General, Lazarini, in protest over the kidnapping of her late son Yonatan by an organization employee (UN WATCH photo) Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

author: BringThemHomeNow
text: Today Yagav Buchstab should have celebrated his 37th birthday, but he will forever remain 35. Yagav was born on January 23, 1989. Eldest son to Oren and Esther, older brother to Nofer and Yuval. A member of Kibbutz Nirim, whose heart was captured by the world of music. When he started learning to play guitar and cello, he revealed himself to be a gifted musician and in his high school years he was even part of a band. Yagav taught himself to play the organ, bagpipes, clarinet and more, each instrument opened up a new and magical world for him. Yagav loved building electric guitars and other instruments together with his brother Yuval. In his adulthood, his love for music led him to study sound, and manage a recording studio. As usual, he didn't give up until every recording was perfect.  Music also brought his lover Rimon into his life. Yagav and Ramon met in their youth in a group where they played together, Yagav as a guitarist and Ramon on drums. About two years before they were kidnapped from their home in Nirim, they got married in the yard of their parents' house. They built their home in Kibbutz Nirim, a home where they raised five dogs and five cats, most of them adopted after being abused.  Along with the sounds, there were also smells of cooking coming from the kitchen of their home. Yagav loved to cook from a young age and the kitchen was for him a place of original creation, experimenting with different techniques and testing new ideas. His family told of a cooking enthusiast who loved meat but also prepared excellent vegan food for the vegan family members. His friends tell with deep longing about Yagave who was a quiet and modest person, interested in a very wide range of subjects: poetry, music, philosophy, politics and more. Self-taught who never stopped expanding knowledge and interest.  On the morning of October 7th, Yagav and Ramon were abducted from their home in the kibbutz, from the MMD, which on normal days was used as the workshop where her son Yagav repaired his guitars. Rimon was released after 53 days as part of the women and children deal. Yagav survived for over 3 months in the tunnels in Gaza and was murdered in captivity.  Today, we will stop for a moment and remember Yagave. A family man, a lover of all living beings who spread sounds in the world that brought light and love.  In his memory 🎗️💛 Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

author: BringThemHomeNow
text: A year ago, the world finally burst with joy as Arbel Yehoud, Agam Berger, and Gadi Moses crossed the border and returned home. Through tears, we watched them fall into the arms of their loved ones.  Since then, we’ve watched them slowly piece their lives back together, bravely sharing some of the ordeals they endured in the hell of Gaza.   They even joined the fight to bring all the hostages home, until the last hostage came back this week 💛  Their strength and courage have helped unite us, the Israeli people and supporters around the world.  Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

Closing a circle is also a concept that I have only experienced, I realized how much these words are just words. You will never close a circle" @eldadarieh @Ronkofman1 Photo: Israel Police Spokesperson Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

author: BringThemHomeNow
text: Tonight, the last rally of the Kibbutz Nir Oz community was held in Carmi Gat. On the day of the announcement of the murder of Kibbutz member Elad Katzir in captivity, the community Nir Oz said: "No more!" and began holding rallies near their temporary residence in Carmi Gat.   Since then, every Shabbat, the community has allowed the families of the abductees and members of the community to participate in a more intimate gathering, closer to their temporary home.  This evening, after the return of the last abductee, Major Ran Goili, the last rally was held in the Gat vineyards. Kibbutz Nir Oz suffered the heaviest blow on October 7 when one out of four members of the kibbutz was murdered or kidnapped. Only 8 houses in the kibbutz remained intact. Photo credit: Uriel Ibn Sapir, Alon Gilboa Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

author: BringThemHomeNow
text: "Today we stop the hands and stop counting the days, hours, minutes and seconds here in the square, this square that the headquarters of the families of the abducted has established for us, the families that were kidnapped to us dear ones."  Michel, the father of Guy Ilouz who was buried after 738 days in captivity, stood in the square today and talked about the cycles of thought and sadness of his family and 45 other families whose loved ones were kidnapped alive and murdered in captivity: "Rehabilitation will not be easy. It will not be quick. You can't really "move on" when there is no chair around the table, when Guy's smile is missing, when his laughter has stopped. But now, when the time of the square has stopped, we can To start measuring a new time. A time of healing, and a time of rebuilding. I would like to thank all those citizens who joined and volunteered for the return of our children. I would like to thank the security forces, the families of the bereaved, and the soldiers who gave up their lives to save the abductees and the state of Israel. Your sacrifice will be in our hearts forever."  Photo credit: Lior Rothstein Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

author: BringThemHomeNow
text: On November 2, 2023, a call went out from the headquarters of the families of the abductees inviting everyone to take part in the empty chair display - until everyone returns home, a yellow chair is placed at the entrance to public areas. Businesses, public and private companies, government bodies and organizations, municipalities, councils and local authorities, educational institutions and cooperative employment buildings - placed a yellow chair at the entrance to their offices. In the main squares of the cities and at the entrance gates of many settlements, displays of chairs with the pictures of the abductees were set up, and the yellow chair also reached the Shabbat and holiday tables in many homes.  The "Ketar" company, which until October 7, 2023 did not market yellow plastic chairs, created during the war 25,000 chairs that were placed across the length and breadth of the country as a symbol of the abductees.   Last weekend, after all 255 abductees from Gaza were resettled, the central display of the yellow chairs was also removed from the abductees' square, but in our hearts all 87 abductees will always remain empty. Those whose chairs remain forever orphaned.  We returned. Now get up.  Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

author: BringThemHomeNow
text: "I came back to life 102 days ago. 102 days in which I'm learning to live again but also learning what was here and how many superheroes there are in the State of Israel. The soldiers, civilians and policemen, among them Ran who you can say tried to save me when he came to the Nova party area from which I was kidnapped."  Captive survivor Segev Kalfon arrived today for the Shabbat reception at Hatavim Square, where he wanted to thank all those who came out on the morning of October 7 to try to rescue, assist and protect the State of Israel: "Ran was supposed to return a long time ago. Ran was not supposed to be kidnapped at all and certainly not to be 738 days in captivity like me, and what is certain is that he was supposed to return with me, in the same deal. Now we are talking about phase two, about continuing and Ran is still there. It could have been me, it's just my luck that I'm here and not there, It's just my luck that there are people like Rani and thanks to that I will be forever grateful to everyone who did everything for me to come back. I just ask that we continue to do everything so that Rani will come back too. For Rani, for the family and for the country that I love so much!  Photo credit: Paulina Fatimer, Uriel Ibn Sapir #ישראלמחקהלרני #אדהחתופהאקרון Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

author: BringThemHomeNow
text: The story of the headquarters of the families for the return of the kidnapped and missing - the dining room (minus 2, more than a floor) With the transition of the headquarters to the Check Point building, the dining room was established on the 2nd floor - for the benefit of the families, volunteers and employees of the headquarters. The dining hall was open between 21:00 and for the benefit of its operation, donations of prepared meals as well as various raw materials flowed in with which dozens of volunteers upgraded the daily menu. When guests would arrive downstairs or at events in the auditorium, there would be volunteers who would provide pampering refreshments.  Each shift was managed by a shift manager with the aim of creating an address for defining tasks, maintaining order and continuity between shifts. Food was served at regular hours, in an aesthetic manner, in abundance, in accordance with the circumstances and the need, with a lot of added emotional value that resulted from the volunteers getting to know the families continuously over months.   Sometimes the members of the families of the abductees would take part in the preparation of the dishes out of their love for the kitchen, something that helped them in the challenging moments of their lives.  Over time, a unique and exciting phenomenon was created that we called the "mamos" - women from settlements throughout the country who took it upon themselves to cook home-made and expensive food for families and volunteers. In addition to the local communities, there were initiatives of sheltered housing chains, parents of school students, workers in workplaces and private families who chose to mark an exciting event such as a birthday by preparing or donating a warm and comforting dinner downstairs.  Very quickly 2- turned from "just a floor" into the heart of the house. The dining room has become a meeting place, a place where hosts, chat with a homely, warm and welcoming atmosphere.  Photos from the 2nd floor - the wonderful, credit to the floor's volunteer team.  Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

author: BringThemHomeNow
text: After recognizing his son, Major Ran Goili, who was returned from Gaza after 843 days, Itzik Goili joined his family members outside the family home in Mitar. There, along with Taliq, Rani's mother, the brothers Omri and Shira, and Sharon, Rani's sister-in-law, the family wanted to thank everyone who took part in the return of Rani, the hero of Israel.  The family thanked the IDF, the Prime Minister, the police and all the people of Israel. In addition, the family members thanked President Trump, the envoy for abductees, Steve Witkoff, and the representative of the American government to the Middle East, Jared Kushner. author: BringThemHomeNow
text: Today Hadar Goldin should have celebrated his 35th birthday, but forever he will remain 23 years old. Hadar, son of Simcha and Lea Goldin, was born on February 18, 1991. Five minutes after he went live, his twin brother Tzur joined him. At the family home, their older brothers were already waiting for them - Ayelet and my father-in-law (Menachem).   Hadar and Tzur brought a lot of light wherever they went. Together they learned to play music, paint and sculpt, together they went to Bnei Akiva and turned from apprentices to instructors and together they went to the "Bnei David" preparatory school with my husband.   When they enlisted in the IDF, their paths diverged, Tsur for the paratroopers and Hadar for the Givat patrol. Hadar was a team leader at the end of the training, a reconnaissance and intelligence course, an officer preparation course, and an officer course in basic training. After the officers' course, he wanted to be a commander in training the patrol's rookies and turn them into fighters. Hadar instilled in his soldiers and subordinates the values he grew up with - friendship Courage among the team members, love and help to others will lead the team to an outstanding team. And then he reached the realization of his ambition - during his military service, Hadar proposed to his girlfriend Edna Sarosi, while he was waiting with his soldiers in the assembly area, and at the same time he arranged the invitation. At 08:00 a.m., a ceasefire was declared shortly after Hamas launched two mortar bombs at 09:05 a.m., and three of the force's soldiers were killed in the battle: Maj. Lial Gideoni. Hadar was kidnapped through a tunnel and held in Gaza for 4,118 days.  Today, we will stop for a moment and we will all remember Lt. Hadar Goldin, who in his smile, in his paintings, in his writings, and in the hearts of his family, apprentices and soldiers, left his will bearing the banner of loving people and doing good. As Hadar himself used to say: "You have two options; either mess with yourself, or do something better."  In his memory 💔 Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

text: One year ago today, Sasha Trupanov, Yair Horn and Shagyi Dekel Chen returned home. With tears we watched them fall into the arms of their loved ones. Read more here: https://bloom.bg/3HkFOYd

author: Bloomberg
text: Tesla is opening its first India showroom as Elon Musk’s electric-vehicle maker looks to ply new markets and offset slowing sales where it’s already well established. More here: https://bloom.bg/44ujSmp

author: Bloomberg
text: 🎙 A Bloomberg investigation shows China is building data centers in the remote Xinjiang region to fuel its AI ambitions — and looking to buy 115,000 Nvidia chips banned by the US to power them.  Listen to the Big Take Asia podcast: https://link.podtrac.com/jxfy2rhy

author: Bloomberg
text: 🎙️ Indian-based workers once supported American financial services firms. Now, they’re increasingly key to their operations.  On today’s Big Take Asia podcast: How India’s government is encouraging Wall Street firms to expand their footprint in India and how President Trump’s new visa policies could speed up the push: https://link.podtrac.com/4rorpntg

author: Bloomberg
text: Chinese electric vehicle brands led by BYD are winning over European customers with sleek, high-tech models at competitive prices.  Now, a startup is looking to muscle in on a more modest market: micro cars. Read more here: https://bloom.bg/3K8JUnB   📷:  Krisztian Bocsi/Bloomberg

author: Bloomberg
text: US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick says a trade deal with India did not materialize last year because Prime Minister Narendra Modi did not call President Donald Trump. https://bloom.bg/49ncFHr  📷: Prakash Singh/Bloomberg

author: Bloomberg
text: 🎙 On today’s Big Take Asia podcast, how a rebel army in Myanmar became a major player in the global supply for rare earths — and what its growing influence means for neighboring China: https://link.podtrac.com/jxfy2rhy

author: Bloomberg
text: American airstrikes had only a limited impact on Iran’s nuclear program, according to early US intelligence findings, as the United Nations watchdog urged fresh inspection of the sites. Read more here: https://bloom.bg/3T7XSat

author: Bloomberg
text: LIVE NOW: Trump is breaking with more than a decade of US policy. Is Washington shifting from strategic partner to trade adversary?  Join Bloomberg reporters for a Live Q&A on what this means: https://bloom.bg/41sPJlr

author: Bloomberg
text: Chen Tao and his wife Liu Chunlan, have become one of China’s richest AI billionaires, as their fortune soar on the world’s insatiable demand for the technology and a critical partnership with Nvidia.  Read more on their combined $9.1 billion net worth, vaulting them above the likes of Bill Ackman and Jon Gray on the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. https://bloom.bg/3KfTeX9

author: Bloomberg
text: Prime Minister Narendra Modi used his first trip to China in seven years to reset relations with India’s powerful neighbor while also seeking to strengthen ties with Russia as President Donald Trump ratchets up tensions with New Delhi. Read more here: https://bloom.bg/4g4ZGfd

author: Bloomberg
text: LATEST: SpaceX’s colossal Starship rocket suffered a leak, tumbled out of control in space and exploded during a test flight, in a third straight major setback for the Elon Musk-led company. Read more here: https://bloom.bg/3T07B2k

author: Bloomberg
text: Singapore's finance industry is synonymous with large-scale electronic banking.  But in a rundown central mall, the city's cash-only money changers buy and sell foreign currency the old-fashioned way — often at better exchange rates than conventional banks. Read more here: https://bloom.bg/4jZvGSg

author: Bloomberg
text: 🎙 China is using domestic hacking competitions to power its growing network of hackers.  Find out what’s at stake for the US and the rest of the world on the Big Take Asia Podcast: https://link.podtrac.com/jxfy2rhy

author: Bloomberg
text: President Donald Trump signed an executive action that prevents foreign nationals from entering the US to study at Harvard University, accusing the school of failing to implement discipline on campus and fostering a dramatic rise in crime. Read more here: https://bloom.bg/4kWYUSJ

author: Bloomberg
text: Human waste, empty oxygen cylinders and kitchen leftovers.  Here's how drones are helping clean the world's highest garbage dump — where Sherpas used to carry kilos of trash down Everest by foot: https://bloom.bg/4lepg34

author: Bloomberg
text: Chinese AI startup MiniMax spent its first three years largely on the sidelines of AI development. While rivals chased local ChatGPT clones, it was tackling a harder problem: building a single model capable of processing text, speech and video. Now, the $619 million IPO crystallizes a surge in wealth for its founder Yan Junjie. https://bloom.bg/3Z4mKmo  📷️: Lam Yik/Bloomberg

author: Bloomberg
text: 🎙 Japan is experiencing an intense talent war as recruiters for Wall Street banks court new hires with increased salaries, fancy dinners and other perks.  Find out more on the Big Take Asia Podcast: https://link.podtrac.com/jxfy2rhy

author: Slavyangrad
text: A message to Washington?  In a tightly structured 12-minute address, Ayatollah Imam Sayyed Mojtaba Khamenei moved from familiar rhetoric into something far more consequential. The opening half followed the expected script; revisiting decades of U.S. warmongering rhetoric: sanctions, assassinations, regional conflicts.  But midway through, the tone shifted from retrospective to strategic.  Sayyed Khamenei outlined three concrete demands, each with a defined timeline: a rapid U.S. military withdrawal from the Middle East, a full rollback of sanctions within 60 days, and long-term financial compensation for economic damages.  Then came the ultimatum. Fail to comply, and Iran escalates, economically, militarily, and potentially nuclearly. Not hypothetically, but operationally: closing the Strait of Hormuz, formalizing defense ties with Russia and China, and moving from ambiguity to declared nuclear deterrence.  The timing of external reactions was just as telling. Within hours, both Beijing and Moscow issued statements aligning, carefully but unmistakably, with Tehran's framing. This definitely looked coordinated.  The broader context matters. Sayyed Mojtaba Khamenei represents a different leadership style from his martyred predecessor leader. Where martyr Sayyed Ali Khamenei operated through long-term balancing and controlled escalation, Sayyed Mojtaba appears positioned to deliver faster, more decisive outcomes.  Iran's internal reports are clear, the Islamic Revolution Guard Corps is in no way, shape or form interested in incrementalism. They are pushing for structural change: removing U.S. influence from the region, restoring Iran's military standing, and forcing a re-negotiation of global power dynamics.  And for the first time in decades, Iran practically has the leverage to  do this.  Rising oil prices, regional instability, growing alignment with China and Russia, and vulnerabilities in global trade routes have shifted the strategic landscape.  So this was not just a speech. It was a test. A test of whether the United States is willing, or even able, to operate under a new set of constraints.  What happens next will likely define not just the trajectory of this conflict, but the broader balance of power in the Middle East for decades to come.

text: As part of NATO's large-scale exercise Cold Response 26, a complex scenario of covert landing of scouts was practiced. Specialists of the reconnaissance and observation squadron of the 30th Commando Regiment of the UK, including a group from the 148th battery, disembarked from a German submarine S185 (Type-212A). The operation was carried out in a covert mode: the personnel with their equipment boarded the submarine using inflatable boats, after which the submarine submerged. After covertly reaching the designated area, the group landed at night to set up an observation post, whose task is to target and adjust the artillery fire of alliance ships.  These exercises are part of a deepening military partnership between the UK and Norway in the Arctic, aimed at countering the Russian Northern Fleet. It is known that the Norwegian Navy is due to receive the first promising anaerobic submarine Type-212CD in 2029 as part of the German-Norwegian program launched in 2023. Its underwater displacement will be 2,800 tons, and its underwater range will significantly increase compared to the Type-212A to participate in operations in the wider North Atlantic and Baltic theaters of operations.  The key element of the success of such operations is the exceptional stealth of the carrier. Type 212A/CD submarines have extremely low acoustic visibility (less than 50 dB in stealth mode) and are equipped with anaerobic air-independent power plants (AIP), allowing them to stay underwater for 20-30 days. This makes their detection in the complex waters of the North Atlantic and Baltic extremely problematic.  In this regard, Russia's non-nuclear submarine fleet is facing a technological gap. Promising projects of non-nuclear submarines, such as the 636.3 "Varshavyanka" and 677 "Lada", have not yet received serial air-independent power plants, which limits their stealth and autonomy. In this regard, the responsible tasks of countering such threats fall primarily on the more modern and low-noise multi-purpose nuclear submarines of Project 885M "Yasen-M".  It is indicative that almost simultaneously with NATO's exercises, Russia's Northern Fleet conducted its own anti-submarine exercise in the Barents Sea. The frigate of Project 22350 "Admiral Golovko" practiced the search for a conditional underwater target using standard hydroacoustic means (the "Zarya-3" hydroacoustic system and the "Vinyekta-EM" hydroacoustic station) and its subsequent destruction with 324-mm torpedoes of the "Paket-NK" complex.  Thus, the Arctic region is becoming an arena for a parallel build-up of capabilities: the alliance is practicing the use of the latest low-noise technologies for covert operations, while Russia is demonstrating its readiness to detect and destroy them in its area of responsibility.  @Slavyangrad

text: 🇺🇸The US is preparing to strike Iran's energy sector. What will this lead to?  Despite the enormous risks, Washington views an attack on Iran's energy system as an effective tool for achieving a number of strategic goals.  First and foremost, strikes on power stations are positioned as a symmetrical response to the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. In this way, the US seeks to demonstrate that the cost of an economic blockade for Iran itself will be higher than for the global market.  It is assumed that without a stable energy supply, the production of ballistic missiles and drones, which Tehran supplies to itself and its proxy groups, will be paralyzed. However, it is not clear yet whether this hypothesis is justified, given the high autonomy of many "missile cities". Moreover, the Trump administration apparently hopes that the economic collapse caused by the lack of electricity and water will be the "last straw" for Iranian society and protests will break out again.  However, there are far more purely economic factors in this strategy. The destabilization of gas and oil supplies from the Middle East makes American liquefied natural gas (LNG) vital for the markets of Europe and Asia. In other words, the US hopes to profit from high oil prices.  However, a political, albeit somewhat reverse effect is also considered inevitable: Iran's retaliatory strikes on the extremely vulnerable energy infrastructure of the Gulf countries (primarily Qatar, the UAE, Bahrain, and Kuwait) will force them to urgently review their own security strategies. However, it is not yet clear where the situation will shift - there is a risk that these countries will start purchasing more US weapons. text: 📚📖 "Europe is now financing Putin's war against Ukraine through oil - and at the same time its protection." World media about the war on March 16 🖌About how Ukrainian technologies for combating drones are beginning to be in increasing demand in the world, writes NBC News. The long war forced Ukraine to constantly test new drone technologies directly on the battlefield. It is thanks to this that a unique system of rapid improvement of drones was formed in the country, said Marko Kushnir, the spokesman of one of the leading Ukrainian drone manufacturers General Chereshnya. "We can get feedback from the military in the morning and come up with a solution in the evening that will help with new tasks on the battlefield," he says.   Now there is a great demand for this experience from other countries: private organizations and governments in the Middle East have already turned to "General Chereshny" for help. That help will include not only the sale of drones, but also the supporting infrastructure they need, such as batteries and maintenance protocols, and most importantly, the experience of using them, Kushnir said.  The attitude of the United States has also changed: back in the summer, a Ukrainian delegation offered the Americans their experience in combating drones, but they became sharply interested in it only after the war with Iran began, said a European official familiar with the matter.  🖌Trump's war with Iran has started a vicious circle: Europe is now indirectly financing Putin's war against Ukraine — and at the same time protecting it. This is stated in an editorial column by Benjamin Bidder for Der Spiegel. The shock of oil prices is a kind of rejuvenating treatment for the "most dangerous adversary of the continent" Vladimir Putin, writes the author of the column. According to him, before the start of the war in the Middle East, the Russian economy had already begun to weaken: revenues from oil and gas fell, budget revenues decreased, large companies were overloaded with debts, and Russia was thinking about reducing public spending.    But now all this can be wasted, because the price of oil has risen - the Russian Urals in some places is even more expensive than Brent. The author of the column claims that Moscow is already receiving billions in additional profits from this situation, and if prices remain high for a long time, Russia will be able to earn approximately $10 billion more every month. This will create a double financial burden for Europe. On the one hand, the rise in global energy prices means more expensive fuel and energy for European economies, which increases Russia's income from oil exports. On the other hand, if Putin's oil revenues continue to grow, so will his ability to wage war against Ukraine — and the European aid package for Ukraine will be exhausted sooner than Brussels expects. text: 🇺🇸🇮🇱🇮🇷 When the US and Israel were planning a war against Iran, they hoped for a quick uprising — but they miscalculated, writes the NYT with reference to more than ten sources.  Before the war, Mossad chief David Barnea presented a plan by which his service could rally the Iranian opposition and incite unrest, leading to the collapse of the Iranian government and the end of the war.  Many high-ranking American officials, as well as analysts of Israel's military intelligence (AMAN), were skeptical of the Mossad's plan. The American military leadership told Trump that the Iranians would not protest until the United States and Israel dropped the bombs. And Trump himself at the beginning of the war advised the Iranians to stay at home and go out only after the end of the air campaign.  Intelligence from both countries now concluded that Iran's theocratic government was weakened but fairly stable, and that fear of Iranian security forces made an uprising less likely. Most likely, the power will be retained by hard-line representatives of the current government.  At the beginning of the war, the US and Israel considered using Kurdish militias from northwestern Iran. However, the US no longer supports this idea — it was opposed by Turkey, which itself is fighting against Kurdish separatists.  @babel

text: 📚📖Ukraine preserved the operation of sea ports during the war - this is what the Persian Gulf countries want to learn. World media about the war on March 19 🖌Despite the blockade of the Black Sea, shelling, mine danger and cyberattacks, Ukraine was able to preserve the operation of its sea ports during the war - now this experience is being carefully studied by other countries, writes Der Spiegel. Against the backdrop of Iran's blockade of oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, port operators in the Persian Gulf countries are trying to understand how Ukraine managed to survive such a blockade and resume maritime trade. "The experience we gained in Ukraine has no analogues," says the head of the Association of Ukrainian Ports, Dmytro Barinov, after speaking to members of the International Association of Ports and Harbors in Odesa.   At first, the Ukrainian military pushed the Russian fleet away from the coast and took control of part of the Black Sea. After that, they launched their own sea corridor closer to the shore — ships with grain went through it, says Barinov. Ports began to work according to a clear schedule: ships enter and leave only at certain times. The military inspects ships while still at sea. Суднам не дозволяють довго стояти в очікуванні — це занадто небезпечно. In the sea, floating barriers were installed that catch mines, and on the territory of the ports - mobile concrete shelters, where workers go in case of alarms. Ports constantly coordinate work with air defense units. After the hacker attacks, part of the processes were transferred to faxes in order not to depend on digital systems.  🖌The biggest threat to Europe right now is Russia and the war against Ukraine, says former NATO Secretary General George Robertson, who headed the Alliance from 1999 to 2003, in an interview with the Finnish public broadcaster Yle. According to him, the support of Kyiv should be the main priority of the Alliance, and if the West is distracted by other crises, in particular in the Middle East, it may have dangerous consequences for the whole of Europe. Ukraine needs more weapons and wider support, and Russia needs to be clearly shown that it cannot win, Robertson notes. He also harshly criticizes Europe's defense policy: despite huge costs, it remains ineffective due to fragmentation and duplication of projects. He emphasizes that Putin only responds to force and determination, so the unity of the US and Europe is crucial.  🖌Foreign Policy publishes an analytical article on the fact that on the eve of the elections in Hungary, Viktor Orbán deliberately avoids a direct fight with the opposition and instead attacks Ukraine in order to change the very essence of the campaign. author: Babel
text: 📚📖 European allies can exchange protection of the Strait of Hormuz for help to Ukraine. World media about the war on March 18 🖌About a possible diplomatic agreement between the USA and Europe, which could simultaneously help solve two international crises - Russia's war against Ukraine and Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, through which almost 20% of the world's oil supplies pass, writes Forbes. With the strait blocked, energy prices have skyrocketed, supplies have become more difficult, and political instability could spread from the Middle East to Europe and Asia, and eventually to the United States. Therefore, the strait should be opened as soon as possible, and the US needs the help of allies, the article says.   The representative of the World Food Program of the United Nations Karl Skau warned: if the war in the Middle East continues until June, another 45 million people could be on the brink of acute hunger due to rising prices. Food shortages will force people to leave their homes. Migration will increase political tensions, and this affects elections, alliances and security policy - primarily in Europe, but also in the US. Therefore, Donald Trump should seriously consider the idea of ​​the President of Finland, Alexander Stubb: Europe will help with the security of the Strait of Hormuz, in return, the United States will promise long-term support to Ukraine. It looks like a transactional agreement and that is why it can work, writes the publication. Trump has long viewed foreign policy as deals rather than doctrines. He called on allies to make more contributions, and he was not too interested in commitments without an expiration date. As the publication writes, such an agreement can be beneficial for both the US and Europe, as it will allow for the distribution of responsibility among the allies and at the same time stabilize the energy situation in the world and strengthen Russia's deterrence.  🗞This is only part of the review. For those who support us on Patreon, summaries of two more materials are available.  #inozmi @babel

text: Approximately 190 million women worldwide have endometriosis. This is a condition in which so-called foci appear in the body - small islands of tissue similar to the uterine mucosa, but located outside it. They can cause unbearable pain during menstruation and many other unpleasant symptoms.  In recent years, the disease has started to be talked about more — thanks to bloggers, stars and even cinema. A documentary about endometriosis, which shows how the disease 'steals time' from normal life, won at the BAFTAs this month.  Women with endometriosis are often stigmatized—for example, that they will not be able to have children. But is it really so? How to detect endometriosis? Can it be cured? "Babel" spoke with specialists of the "Dobrobut" medical network.  @babel

text: The Russians attacked Ukraine again. Here is what is known about the consequences of shelling: 🔴Kharkivshchyna. As a result of the impact of the FPV drone, emergency medical personnel were injured: a 57-year-old paramedic and a 31-year-old driver. The car is damaged.  Kherson. author: Babel
text: Today, the sociological group "Rating" presented a large sociological study. Its focus is on Ukrainian youth (ages 14-35), including those who have moved abroad.  In Ukraine, sociologists covered residents of front-line territories and rural areas, veterans, and displaced persons — but not those who serve in the Defense Forces. Sociologists interviewed 600 young Ukrainians in 24 countries abroad.  In both groups, the researchers asked about mental health, professional skills and priorities, national identity, attitudes towards mobilization and emigration or return to the country.  The editor of "Babel" Hleb Gusev selected the thirteen most interesting results that relate to the most painful issues. Here's what they look like.  @babel

author: Babel
text: 🇺🇦🇬🇧 Ukraine and Britain will conclude an agreement on military partnership in the field of drones and AI, according to the website of the British government.  The agreement provides for joint work on combating drones. Ukraine will share combat experience, and Britain - production capabilities.  They plan to develop and produce drones, in particular interceptor drones. The countries also want to expand cooperation with other states.  Separately, Great Britain is investing about $667,000 in the creation of the Center of Excellence in the field of AI, which will work under the Ministry of Defense of Ukraine.  @babel

author: Babel
text: Astronomers have discovered a planet where the surface is a continuous ocean of magma. She is not like any known today.  It is about the exoplanet L98-59d, located approximately 35 light years from Earth. It is 1.6 times larger than our planet and revolves around a small red star.  At first, scientists assumed that there could be an ocean of water on it. But new research has shown otherwise: beneath the surface, there probably stretches a giant ocean of magma, thousands of kilometers long, that may even include a molten core.  The temperature on the surface can reach about 1,900°C, and the atmosphere probably contains a lot of hydrogen sulfide, a gas with the smell of rotten eggs.  Researchers believe that this discovery may indicate the existence of a whole new class of planets. Such worlds may be much more common than previously thought, prompting scientists to reassess which exoplanets might be habitable.  @babel

author: Babel
text: 🇺🇸 Donald Trump said that NATO faces a "very bad future" if US allies do not help unblock the Strait of Hormuz.  The day before, he made such a request to Great Britain, France, China, Japan and South Korea - because, according to him, Europe and China are highly dependent on oil from the Persian Gulf, unlike the USA.  Trump also said he may postpone a meeting with Chinese leader Xi Jinping in late March if China does not help lift its blockade of Iran.  British Prime Minister Keir Starmer refused to send warships. Reluctance was also expressed by France, Germany, South Korea, Japan and Australia.  ▪️After the start of the war between Israel, the USA and Iran, the latter actually blocked the Strait of Hormuz, through which about 20% of the world's oil passes. Currently, Brent oil costs about $104, which is about 45% higher than it was before the war.  @babel

author: Babel
text: Centers for training humanoid robots are opening in China, writes Interesting Engineering.  More than 40 state centers for training such robots have been created, 24 of them are already working. In Shandong province, robots are taught to carry objects, fold clothes, and more.  In other centers, they sort materials and pack goods. Therefore, experts literally show the robots every movement: how the joints work, what speed and strength should be.  Humanoids are expected to be used initially in industry and logistics. There, they will perform simple and repetitive tasks that humans do now.  Photo: Getty Images @babel

author: Babel
text: 💥 The General Staff confirmed the night attack on the Transnafta - Port Primorsk oil terminal in the Leningrad region.  According to preliminary information, the tank and oil infrastructure were hit. The fire continues.  About 60 million tons of oil pass through the port of Primorsk every year - it is the main Russian oil export hub on the Baltic Sea.  💥 The Bashnafta-Ufanaftakhim refinery in Bashkortostan was also attacked, approximately 1,400 km from the border with Ukraine.  A fire started on its territory. The capacity of this oil refinery is 6-8 million tons per year.  @babel

author: Babel
text: Fuel cashback has started working in Ukraine as of today.  Partial compensation can be obtained for the purchase of fuel at gas stations participating in the program. 15% cashback on diesel, 10% on gasoline, 5% on autogas.  This will save from 2 to 11 hryvnias per liter. The maximum amount of cashback is up to UAH 1,000 per person per month.  The program will work until May 1 within the framework of "National Cashback". The money can be used to pay for utilities, medicine, Ukrainian-made products, books, postal services, or to support the Ukrainian military.  ▪️The prices of oil, gas and precious metals jumped due to the war between Iran, Israel and the USA. The price of Brent oil has increased by 50% - it is now worth more than $108 per barrel.   @babel

author: Babel
text: Donald Trump has threatened to destroy Iran's power plants if it does not open the Strait of Hormuz in the next two days.  Iran responded by vowing to attack all energy and IT infrastructure, as well as desalination plants linked to the US and Israel in the Middle East.  ▪️After the start of the war between Israel, the USA and Iran, the latter actually blocked the Strait of Hormuz, through which about 20% of the world's oil passes. Currently, Brent oil costs about $112, which is about 40% higher than it was before the war.  @babel

author: Babel
text: 🇮🇪 In Ireland, a 31-year-old Ukrainian man was fatally stabbed with a knife when he went out to buy groceries, writes The Irish Times.  The attack took place in the evening of March 17. Despite severe injuries, the Ukrainian was able to walk about 100 meters to his house and immediately fainted.  It was not possible to save the man - he died from his injuries. The deceased was born in Ukraine, but lived most of his adult life in Ireland.  The next day, the police detained the suspect, a man in his 40s. The police consider the attack accidental.  Photo: Daragh Mc Sweeney / Provision @babel

author: Babel
text: In the Kyiv Zoo, Mo the muntjac recovered after a severe injury received as a result of the shelling of the Russians in November 2025.  The broken jaw has grown together, and he already tastes young grass and green twigs.  Also, Mo and Milo had a munchkin. You can see them on the ungulate row of the zoo near the "Desert" pavilion.  ▪️Muntjak, or barking deer, is a genus of deer common in South and Southeast Asia, in China and some areas of Japan.   @babel

author: Babel
text: Prices for Russian Urals oil in India reached a record level — $98.93 per barrel, Bloomberg writes.  This is the highest figure since Russia diverted a significant portion of its oil exports to India after a full-scale invasion of Ukraine.  The increase in prices occurred against the background of the increase in the price of oil in the world due to the war in the Middle East. At the same time, the discount on Russian oil delivered to Indian ports decreased to $4.80 per barrel.  ▪️Last ​​week, the US Treasury issued a license that allows buyers to buy oil from the Russian Federation that is already at sea. Earlier, the exemption from sanctions was valid only for India, but now it has been extended to other countries.  @babel

author: Babel
text: The Russians once again attacked Ukraine with missiles and drones. Here is what is known about the consequences: 🔴Daughter. As a result of the Russian attack on Mykolaivka, Kramatorsk district, one person was killed and another was injured. Damaged high-rise building.  🔴Gloomy. A Russian unmanned aerial vehicle hit the cab of a truck loaded with grain in Sadivska hromada, killing a 40-year-old man.  🔴 Zaporozhye. During the Russian shelling, a woman died, three more people were injured. A Russian unmanned aerial vehicle destroyed a one-story building.  🔴Dnipropetrovsk region. Two people died as a result of the shelling of the Zaitsivska community. 10 private houses and an educational institution were damaged.  @babel

author: Babel
text: 🇮🇷 Iran has arrested 97 people accused of working for Israel, Reuters writes.  This happened as part of a large-scale security campaign, during which hundreds of people have been detained since February 28 on suspicion of ties to Israel and the United States.  Iranian state media also quoted the police commander of Alborzh province as saying that 41 people had been detained for sending videos to foreign opposition media.  @babel

author: Babel
text: Elon Musk misled Twitter investors during a deal to buy the company in 2022, a jury has found.  According to the jury, Musk's public statements and tweets — specifically about the large number of bots and the "pause" in the deal — influenced the market and artificially depressed the stock's value.  Musk himself insisted that he was not misleading investors, but that people were simply taking his public comments and tweets too literally.  Photo: Getty Images / "Babel" @babel

author: Babel
text: Last year, Russia stole 2 million tons of Ukrainian grain, the head of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine, Andriy Sybiga, said.  The Russian Federation sold it to Africa, Asia, the Middle East and even Europe. About 40% went to Egypt.  In addition, Sybiga said that in recent months, Russia has attacked the infrastructure of the Odesa port more than in all previous years.  @babel
