author: United24Media
text: The largest port on the Baltic Sea, Primorsk in Russia’s Leningrad region, was attacked by drones.  The strike caused a fuel tank to catch fire, said Governor Alexander Drozdenko.  He also claimed that dozens of drones targeted the region, with Russian air defense allegedly shooting down about 60 UAVs in less than 24 hours.  The port of Primorsk is Russia’s largest oil port on the Baltic Sea, with a capacity of up to 75 million tons per year. A significant share of Urals crude is exported from there, including via the shadow fleet.

text: ❗️For three consecutive months, Russian battlefield losses have exceeded the number of newly recruited soldiers, Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine Oleksandr Syrskyi said.  At the moment, the Kremlin has no intention of stopping offensive operations, despite suffering significant losses on the battlefield, which for three months in a row have exceeded the rate of replenishment of the Russian army, he noted.

author: United24Media
text: ❗️British Prime Minister Keir Starmer and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy signed a declaration on enhanced cooperation in the field of security and defense in London.  The declaration states that the two countries will work to develop a joint defense-industrial and technological ecosystem. This cooperation may include the creation of joint production lines, joint research and development, the integration of defense supply chains, and the development of industrial partnerships.

author: United24Media
text: Iran has threatened Ukraine with strikes.  The head of the Iranian parliament’s National Security Committee, Ebrahim Azizi, said Ukraine’s entire territory could be considered a legitimate target for attacks.  “By supporting the Israeli regime with drones, the collapsed Ukraine has effectively found itself involved in a war and, in accordance with Article 51 of the UN Charter, has turned its entire territory into a legitimate target for Iran,” he said.

text: A memorial event was held in Milan for the victims of the Russian airstrike on the Mariupol Drama Theater.  Exactly four years ago, the occupiers dropped bombs on a building where more than a thousand civilians were hiding, killing at least 600 people.  Participants in the “Souls of Mariupol” flash mob lined up in the square, forming a huge “CHILDREN” inscription with their bodies — the same one civilians made in front of the theater in 2022.  “Memory is a duty. Memory is justice,” noted the Boristene Cultural Association.  📹: boristene_associazione/Instagram

text: India may abandon the Russian Su-57, Defense Express reports.  New Delhi is considering joining European projects such as Tempest or FCAS. The decision is based on its 2018 experience, when India withdrew from a joint program with Russia due to the aircraft not meeting requirements.  India is currently focusing on its own AMCA project and the purchase of French Rafale jets. Investments in a sixth-generation program could reach €12.5–16.5 billion, making the Su-57 economically and technologically less viable.  According to experts, such a move could significantly weaken Russia’s position in the global arms market.

text: 🇷🇸 Serbia has purchased Chinese ballistic missiles, saying it is preparing for a possible attack from Croatia and Albania.  Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić confirmed that the country has acquired Chinese CM-400AKG missiles and modified its MiG-29 fighter jets to carry them.  According to him, Serbia has become the first European operator of these weapons and already possesses a “significant number” of missiles.  Croatia criticized the deal, calling it a threat to regional stability and a sign of an arms race in the Balkans.  Vučić said Serbia is preparing for a possible attack from Croatia, Albania, and Kosovo, which he claimed are “waiting for chaos in the world to attack.”  The CM-400AKG is a supersonic missile with a range of up to 400 km and can carry a warhead weighing 150–200 kg.

text: ❗️The European Union has imposed sanctions on nine Russian commanders involved in war crimes in Bucha.  The highest-ranking official on the list is Alexander Chaiko. At the beginning of the invasion, he commanded the Eastern Military District and was the main Russian commander in the area during the occupation of Bucha.  Sanctions were also imposed on officers who led units in Hostomel, Irpin, and Borodianka. One of the individuals is also involved in the illegal adoption of a child deported from the occupied part of Donetsk region.  The restrictions include an asset freeze in the EU, a ban on entry and transit, and a ban on EU citizens and companies providing them with financial services.

text: Iran attacked a branch of the American bank Citibank in Dubai in response to US and Israeli strikes on banks in Tehran.  “If the enemy repeats a similar strike, all branches of US banks in the region will become legitimate targets for us,” said a representative of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, General Ali Mohammad Naini.

author: United24Media
text: Large-scale NATO exercises involving about 30,000 troops have begun in Norway and Finland.  According to BILD, the large-scale NATO exercise Cold Response has started in the two countries. About 30,000 troops from 14 alliance states are taking part in the maneuvers, including around 4,000 from the United States and more than 1,500 from Germany.  Politicians will also observe the drills. The German chancellor will meet with the prime ministers of Norway and Canada and visit the Andøya Space Center and the Bardufoss military base, where the exercises are taking place.

author: United24Media
text: “I am grateful to the 35 MEPs for expressing a clear position on Hungary’s banditry, the detention and ill-treatment of seven Ukrainian citizens last week, as well as the theft of money and gold from the state-owned Oschadbank,” Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said.  “Such a strong statement reflects a principled European position in defense of the rule of law and our common values.  The lawlessness in Hungary has crossed all possible limits, and it must be spoken about, not tolerated.  In this regard, we rely on strong voices in Europe that take a principled position.”

author: United24Media
text: “They didn’t even see us”: Ukrainian forces defeated their opponents during NATO naval exercises off the coast of Portugal.  A multinational naval group commanded by Ukrainians penetrated the “enemy’s” defenses during the NATO exercise REPMUS/Dynamic Messenger 2025 and “sank” at least one allied frigate before it even realized it had been destroyed.  Five scenarios off the coast of Portugal practiced defending ports and convoys, as well as attacking convoys. In all five scenarios, the “Reds,” led by the Ukrainians, defeated the NATO naval forces’ “Blues” using Magura V7 naval drone.  During one scenario, a simulated attack on a convoy reportedly hit a frigate so many times that it would have sunk in a real battle. Five minutes later, the “Blues” unsuspectingly asked in the general chat: “So, are you going to attack us now or not?”  A Ukrainian source commented: “The problem wasn’t that they couldn’t stop us—they didn’t even see us.” A NATO spokesman confirmed to Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung that during these exercises, for the first time in the alliance’s history, the Ukrainian navy led and coordinated the actions of the “enemy,” calling it “a historic milestone that confirms Ukraine’s growing role in NATO exercises.”

author: United24Media
text: Hungary will block the provision of a €90 billion EU loan to Ukraine and the adoption of the 20th package of EU sanctions against Russia as long as Ukraine blocks the transit of Russian oil through the Druzhba pipeline, Hungarian Foreign Minister Péter Szijjártó said.

But since Kyiv is not ready for this, we will pursue the goals of the ‘SVO’ on the ground, which is currently happening,” said Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov.  ▫️ Since 2022, Russia has been committed to all agreements on a political and diplomatic settlement of the Ukrainian crisis, but they are being sabotaged by the Ukrainian side;  ▫️ Moscow will not be satisfied with a settlement of the Ukrainian conflict that presupposes the retention of the current authorities;  ▫️ The EU has completely discredited itself; its position contains nothing constructive for progress in the Ukraine negotiations;  ▫️ The official French representative who arrived in Moscow to establish political contacts on the Ukrainian settlement brought nothing new;  ▫️ Moscow assumes that the understanding reached with Belgrade on preventing Serbian arms supplies to Kyiv remains in force.

text: NAVI won the prestigious ESL Pro League Season 23 in Counter-Strike 2.   In the final, NAVI defeated Aurora 3–1 to become the competition champion.  The total prize pool for the tournament was approximately $776,000, with $275,000 going to the players of the winning team.  With this victory, NAVI became the fifth organization in the world to win three ESL Pro League titles.

author: United24Media
text: Russia is considering restricting the operation of foreign AI models, including ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini, according to Russian media.  The official reason is to “protect citizens” from alleged hidden manipulation and discriminatory algorithms.  At the same time, services with more than 500,000 daily users would be required to store Russian citizens’ data within the country for up to three years. Chinese models such as Qwen and DeepSeek are also being considered for adaptation and use as alternatives to Western systems.

author: United24Media
text: Russia’s budget is coming apart at the seams. The war is extraordinarily expensive for Russia, and unlike Ukraine, it has no partners to help carry the burden. Its only real lifeline is the price of oil, which is why it is so important to preserve sanctions against Russia and prevent the Kremlin from turning oil revenues into ballistic missiles.

author: United24Media
text: In Sumy, Russian forces struck rescuers, damaging a fire truck, the State Emergency Service reported.  “On the night of March 22, SES personnel were conducting another inspection of the area after an enemy strike.  As the rescuers were preparing to return to their unit, the enemy struck again near the fire tanker.  Fortunately, the personnel reacted in time and moved to a safe location,” the statement said.

author: United24Media
text: Yesterday, a Ukrainian thermal imaging company, Archer LPP, was set on fire in the Czech Republic.  A group calling itself “Earthquake Faction,” described as pro-Palestinian activists, claimed responsibility for the arson, stating its intention to target weapons production linked to Israel.

author: United24Media
text: Volodymyr Zelenskyy said that Russia must clearly understand and truly feel that Ukraine will be part of European Union and that this cannot be stopped.  According to him, Ukraine is carrying out internal reforms and working externally to secure a clear date for EU accession.  “If a clear date is set, it will mean that Russia will not be able to block our accession in any way. You see how various things are blocked and how difficult it is for a united Europe to implement even decisions that have already been made. This must not happen with the opening of clusters for Ukraine or with our accession — this is a matter of trust, security, and the future,” the President said at a European Council meeting.

author: United24Media
text: In India, crematoriums have stopped using gas for cremations, and restaurants have been advised to avoid dishes that require long cooking times or deep frying because of the war in the Middle East, the Financial Times reports.  A severe energy crisis has emerged in South Asia. The region is heavily dependent on gas supplies from the Persian Gulf, which have been disrupted by the war in the Middle East.  In Mumbai, about one-fifth of establishments have already closed. Up to half could shut down if supplies are not restored. Authorities have temporarily allowed the use of more polluting fuels — coal, wood, and kerosene.  In Pakistan, government agencies have switched to a four-day work week. Schools are closed until the end of the month, and universities have moved classes online.  In Bangladesh, where about 95% of energy is imported, large-scale gas rationing has been introduced. Universities are closed, exams have been cancelled, and energy-saving measures have been implemented in government buildings.  Long queues have formed at petrol stations in Sri Lanka, as the country can store enough liquefied gas for only about a week.

author: United24Media
text: North Korea earned between $7.67 billion and $14.4 billion from sending troops and weapons to the Russian Federation, according to a report by the Institute for National Security Strategy of South Korea.  The report states that the amount of foreign currency received from the four waves of troop deployments is estimated at $620 million.  The amount of foreign currency received from exporting various artillery systems, shells, and ballistic missiles between August 2023 and December 2025 is estimated at $7.05–13.78 billion.  A significant part (80–96%) of the compensation was or will be received in the form of sensitive military technologies, precision components, and related materials.  The report says that if North Korea receives the full amount for troop deployments and arms exports, the main economic effect of sanctions against the DPRK — a reduction in foreign currency revenues — would be neutralized.  It predicts that, if cooperation continues, North Korea could earn $560 million annually from troop deployments alone. However, the confirmed compensation received so far is estimated at about 4–19.6% of the projected income.  According to the British Open Source Centre and the Russian media outlet Important Stories, since the summer of 2023, four Russian ships have made at least 112 trips to the DPRK, delivering between 8 and 11 million rounds of ammunition to the Russian Federation.  On average, Russia received about 350,000 rounds per month, allowing it to maintain the pace of offensive operations.  The companies “MG-Flot” and “Sovfrakht” were involved in supplies from the DPRK. The owner of 50% of MG-Flot shares, Jamaldin Pashayev, is under US sanctions for importing drone components from Iran to Russia.

text: Russian forces attacked the port of Odesa with drones overnight.  Two people were injured in the strikes.  Two civilian commercial vessels, flying the flags of Palau and Barbados, were damaged while moored at the piers and loaded with grain.  Administrative buildings, a grain bunker, and equipment were also damaged. The fires have already been extinguished.

text: Putin’s philosopher Aleksandr Dugin suggested that Russians live like bears.  He proposed that Russians should completely turn off the internet in the spring to live a “real human life,” which, in his view, means adapting to the seasonal cycles of “bears and butterflies.”  He said that when it’s warm, there should be no internet because life is happening, but in winter people could return online, as if coming out of a den.

text: During his interview with Caolan Robertson, President Zelenskyy discussed why the US turns to Ukraine for help in defending its military bases against Iran. He emphasized that, thanks to the level of technological development and the hard work of the Ukrainian people, Ukraine “has the cards” now. Even more, it had them all along, but like any good player, it wasn't showing them.

Over the past few days, fighters of the State Border Guard Service of Ukraine have discovered and destroyed two Grad MLRS. In addition, the enemy lost several artillery guns, as well as dozens of attack drone and UAV operators.  Border guards also tracked down and destroyed several drone control positions — along with the pilots.

text: 🇪🇺🇺🇦 The European Commission has offered Ukraine a mission to inspect the Druzhba pipeline, while there is no information about a Hungarian delegation in Brussels.  “We are conducting intensive discussions and contacts with Ukraine on this issue, as has been the case for several weeks, as well as with the member states that are most concerned (Hungary and Slovakia). I can report that we have offered a mission to Ukraine to inspect the pipeline. I have no information about the Hungarian delegation,” said EC energy spokesperson Anna-Kaisa Itkonen.  She added that the European Commission is currently waiting for a response and remains in contact with Ukrainian authorities and other member states.

text: The United States has announced the lifting of sanctions against Belaruskali, the Belarusian Ministry of Finance, and the Development Bank of Belarus.  U.S. Special Envoy John Cole said the restrictions have been permanently lifted, including measures against the potash industry introduced in 2021. The decision to ease sanctions was announced in December 2025.  The move is linked to agreements between the United States and Belarus, under which Minsk released a number of political prisoners. According to the U.S., this includes more than 200 people.  Trump’s special envoy also said that preparations are underway for a visit by Alexander Lukashenko to the United States.

author: United24Media
text: 🚫👏 22 countries demand that Russia be removed from the 2026 Venice Biennale.  The letter was signed by representatives of Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Spain, Ireland, Lithuania, Latvia (initiators of the letter), Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Sweden, and Ukraine.  They stressed that culture cannot be a platform for the “soft power” of an aggressor state.  Ukraine’s Minister of Culture, Tetyana Berezhna, noted that Russia is planning a performance about “culture beyond politics,” involving two Ukrainians from occupied Crimea.  “Russia is trying to normalize the war and normalize the terrible crimes it is committing. But this is a very dangerous signal that we are fighting against,” she said.  The day before, the European Commission had already threatened the Biennale Foundation with sanctions for allowing an aggressor state to participate.

author: United24Media
text: Defenders of Kostiantynivka showed the destruction of the city under constant attacks by Russian forces.  Fighters of the 24th Separate Mechanized Brigade, who are holding the defense on the eastern approaches to Kostiantynivka, shared photos of the city, which continues to suffer daily strikes.  The city is steadily being destroyed. Aerial bombs, artillery, and drones are erasing block after block. Only the foundations remain of some buildings, the Ukrainian defenders said.  Russian FPV drones are actively targeting transport and people, including both military personnel and civilians moving around the city.  The evacuation of local residents has become almost impossible due to constant shelling of access roads.

author: United24Media
text: The escalation in the Middle East has forced the world to view Ukraine differently, Foreign Ministry spokesman Heorhii Tykhyi said.  Tykhyi noted that the escalation in the Persian Gulf could accelerate Ukraine’s conclusion of drone agreements and change global perceptions of the country.  According to him, Iran’s confrontation with the United States and Israel highlights Ukraine’s unique experience, making it a valuable partner.  He also referred to remarks by Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha, who said that countries in the region, forced to defend themselves against Iranian drones, now see Ukraine not as a requester of aid, but as a strong military force.  Tykhy also recalled a statement by President Volodymyr Zelenskyy about Ukraine’s readiness to develop security cooperation with the United States, NATO, and other partners.

author: United24Media
text: 📱 “Shows the front in real time.” Volodymyr Zelenskyy spoke about the iPad he gave to Charles III.  The president and Ukraine’s military leadership use iPads to track the situation on the front in real time. The device allows them to monitor large-scale attacks by Russia, control movements, and check data on enemy losses.  The president presented such an iPad to King Charles III during his visit. Similar devices are used by the prime minister, the minister of defense, and the command of the Armed Forces of Ukraine.  The head of state said the monarch asked whether he had another such device. The president replied that he only had one, to which King Charles said he would share it with Prime Minister Keir Starmer.

author: United24Media
text: ❗️The Russian Armed Forces launched a spring–summer offensive in the Zaporizhzhia region, deploying infantry, armored vehicles, motorcycles, and even horses, according to Robert "Madyar" Brovdi.  Russian forces attempted to use fog as cover, but their reliance on “invisibility” failed — Ukrainian troops engaged the assault groups as they approached.  In the past day alone, more than 500 Russian soldiers were killed and wounded. Overall, more than 900 casualties have been reported over the past 1.5 days in the Rodinske–Huliaipole sector.  According to military reports, the enemy failed to break through the front line.

author: United24Media
text: A large convoy of trucks labeled as “Humanitarian Aid” has departed Tajikistan for Iran, drawing scrutiny amid documented defense ties between Tehran and Dushanbe and broader concerns over regional logistics networks.  The convoy raises a key question about its contents, given the lack of transparency, Tajikistan’s role in Iranian drone production, and well‑established Central Asian transit routes also used for Russia–Iran logistics.  The development has prompted comparisons to Russia’s covert military supply operations in Ukraine during the early phase of its 2014 invasion. Russia transferred weapons, ammunition, and military equipment to Ukraine's Donetsk region under the guise of humanitarian aid.

After the victory, Mochulskyi thanked everyone who gives him the opportunity to represent Ukraine on the international stage and raise the national flag. He also expressed gratitude to his comrades for their support and to the command for their trust, the Western Regional Department of the State Border Guard Service of Ukraine reported.

text: ❗️Germany is temporarily simplifying arms exports to Ukraine and Gulf states to strengthen air and maritime defense.  The German Ministry of Economics said the new AGG 48 permit will be valid until September 15 and allows deliveries without prior approval for each application. It covers air defense systems and countermeasures against sea mines.  The list of countries includes Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain, Oman, and Ukraine.  Exporters must register within 30 days of the first delivery and submit monthly export reports.

Tokyo will make a final decision after comparing the characteristics of Ukrainian drones with analogues from other countries, in particular from Israel. However, due to the political situation around the Gaza Strip, the Japanese authorities are inclined to support Ukrainian developments, sources told the publications.

text: President Zelenskyy said that Ukraine and European countries are working to seize oil from vessels of Russia’s shadow fleet.  “While the war continues, pressure on the aggressor must also continue. We are working with European countries so that their legal frameworks allow not only stopping such vessels, but also blocking them and seizing the oil,” he said in an evening address on March 21.  Zelenskyy added that despite sanctions imposed by Ukraine, United Kingdom, the European Union, and the United States on a shadow fleet tanker detained by French naval forces, Russia continues to use it.

author: United24Media
text: 🇩🇪🇺🇦 Germany has transferred a new batch of interceptor missiles for the Patriot air defense system to Ukraine, the Ministry of Defense reported.  PAC-3 missiles are capable of intercepting Kinzhal, Iskander, and Zircon missiles.  Key features of the PAC-3:  ▪️ destroys targets with a direct kinetic hit (hit-to-kill); ▪️ speed up to 6,170 km/h; ▪️ range up to 45 km, interception altitude up to 12 km; ▪️ active homing, which does not require constant target illumination; ▪️ a Patriot launcher equipped with PAC-3 can destroy up to 16 targets without reloading.  Strengthening air defense remains a key task of Ukraine’s War Plan. The goal is to detect 100% of threats and intercept at least 95% of missiles and drones, the ministry added.

text: New footage shows an improvised Armored Repair and Evacuation Vehicle of the 57th Separate Motorized Infantry Brigade, created from a hybrid of the hull of a captured 2S19 “Msta-S” and a turret from a T-72B. author: United24Media
text: The European Commission has urged EU member states to speed up efforts to fill gas storage, the Financial Times reports.  In a letter seen by the publication, EU Energy Commissioner Dan Jørgensen called on governments to lower their storage target to 80% capacity, 10 percentage points below the bloc’s official level.  Jørgensen also advised countries to begin gradually refilling reserves to avoid a “summer rush” that could put additional pressure on the market.

author: United24Media
text: Ukraine’s Defense Ministry intelligence (HUR) confirmed that the UAV wreckage found on Independence Square after the March 16 attack on Kyiv was a Lancet.  “The remains of the UAV were identified as a Lancet, which may indicate that the enemy has modernized this weapon. Previously, its main purpose was to destroy vehicles, equipment, and firing positions at tactical and operational depth.  In the Lancet, the enemy is trying to implement elements of autonomous guidance using artificial intelligence modules, including solutions based on Nvidia Jetson. Similar technologies were previously detected in other enemy UAVs — V2U,” the intelligence service said.  Russia receives most of the components used to produce Lancets from abroad, primarily from the United States, as well as from Switzerland and China.  “Despite sanctions, Russia retains access to critical technologies and continues to improve its weapons. Even technological products such as modules for AI-based solutions remain available to it,” the intelligence officers concluded.

author: United24Media
text: Alessandro Giuli, Italy’s culture minister, has called for the resignation of the government’s representative on the Venice Biennale council, Tamara Gregoretti, over Russia’s possible return.  He said he had lost confidence in Gregoretti because she had not informed the ministry about the issue, despite its “international sensitivity.”  The ministry stressed that the decision to admit Russia was taken independently by the Biennale’s organizing committee and contradicts the position of the Italian government.  Ukraine, Lithuania, and 20 other European countries have already officially condemned the move, while the European Commission has threatened sanctions. More than 8,000 cultural figures have signed a petition against the “normalization of war crimes through art,” calling for the closure of the Russian pavilion.

author: United24Media
text: 🇺🇦🇫🇷 LITKOVSKA conquered Paris Fashion Week with a collection about the indomitable Kyiv this winter.  The Ukrainian brand entered the main schedule of Paris Fashion Week for the first time, presenting the Autumn–Winter 2026/27 collection called FIREFLY.  According to designer Lilia Litkovska, the collection was inspired by winter Kyiv during blackouts.  “In Kyiv, there are days without electricity, without heat, without water. People move around the city with small flashlights on their heads. From afar, the streets resemble a sky that has fallen to the ground — scattered with moving tiny stars, fireflies. It was this image that became the soul of the collection.  FIREFLY explores the idea of an inner light that does not fade under the pressure of circumstances and unites people even in times of uncertainty,” Litkovska shared.  This image became the central idea of the show — an inner light that does not go out even in the dark.  A special feature of the presentation was a fragrance created together with a perfumer, designed to convey the smell of winter Kyiv — cold air, stone, smoke, and human presence.  Throughout the show, the flashlight appears both as a practical object and as a metaphor for direction and survival.  “When there is darkness around, one light helps another find the way,” the brand representatives added.

author: United24Media
text: Ukrainian Foreign Ministry spokesman Heorhii Tykhyi said that Hungary is politicizing the issue of repairing the Druzhba pipeline.  He added that instead of explaining to Hungarian citizens why the country has failed to diversify its energy supplies, Prime Minister Viktor Orbán is focusing his rhetoric on Ukraine.  “And even after the damage to the Druzhba pipeline, other Ukrainian pipelines and infrastructure have also been damaged, including the Odesa–Brody pipeline. Ukraine is repairing all this, but we do not have unlimited resources. We are in a state of full-scale war, which Hungary for some reason prefers to ignore,” Tykhyi said.

author: United24Media
text: “We need negotiations. We support them. We don’t trust Russia, but I think and believe that the Americans really want to end this war. I hope they will help us, but we need more pressure on Russia, not on me,” Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in an interview with Politico.  Other key points:  ▫️ The Ukrainian people are tired, but their morale remains high. Ukrainians are not ready to accept Russian ultimatums to hand over significant territories in the east of the country.  ▫️ It is very important for Ukraine what the security guarantees will look like, but there is still no clear answer.  ▫️ President Trump said to me: “Do you trust that our security guarantees can be stronger than NATO?” I replied: “Yes, it depends on you today. It depends on you, Mr. President. God grant that we receive security guarantees stronger than NATO. But what will happen after you? And what will happen after me?”  ▫️ No final agreements have been reached yet, and any negotiations are likely to be very delicate.  ▫️ Trump is right when he says that Putin and I hate each other. He is right about that. But not about everything.  ▫️ The European Union should prepare a Plan B if Viktor Orbán’s blackmail cannot be overcome before Kyiv runs out of resources.  ▫️ Diplomatic silence is not very useful in relations with the Hungarian prime minister.  ▫️ Orbán is on the side of the Russian leader. He is doing the same thing — blocking everything for Ukraine. He is also spreading Russian narratives — the same narratives — and doing it personally. The only thing he is not doing today is attacking our territory with missiles or drones. And he is not sending his military.

text: The State Emergency Service showed the consequences of the attack on the Kyiv region.  Fires were recorded in four districts of the region:  • In Brovary, warehouses and production facilities were hit. A dormitory building was damaged, and firefighters are extinguishing a blaze in an office building. In the village of Pohreby, the roof of a restaurant caught fire; • In the village of Novi Petrivtsi, Vyshhorod district, warehouses caught fire; • Private houses were burning in Obukhiv, and in the town of Ukrainka, Obukhiv district, the roof of a nine-story building caught fire after debris fell; • In the village of Stoianka, Bucha district, rescuers extinguished a fire in a private house.  The National Police reported that the death toll in the region has risen to four, and 10 people were injured. In Brovary alone, three people were killed and eight others were injured.

text: Ukrainian military personnel placed second at international cyber exercises in Singapore.  A joint team of cybersecurity units of the Armed Forces of Ukraine and the 21st Signal Regiment of the United Kingdom won silver at the Defense Cyber Marvel 2026 exercises.  More than 2,500 specialists from 29 countries took part in the competition, organized by the British Ministry of Defence.  Participants practiced protecting military systems, cloud services, and critical infrastructure from complex, multi-level attacks.

In Bucharest, the head of state will meet with President Nicușor Dan, Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan, and visit the F-16 pilot training center.  A joint press conference of the two presidents is expected.

author: United24Media
text: Iran attacked a key oil refinery in Saudi Arabia, posing new threats to global oil supplies, according to Reuters.  The SAMREF refinery in the Saudi port city of Yanbu on the Red Sea was hit. The facility, owned by Saudi Aramco and ExxonMobil, processes oil and prepares fuel for export.  According to the agency, citing sources, the damage was minimal, but the attack itself is significant due to Yanbu’s role in the global energy sector. Following the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, the port has become one of the main alternative routes for oil exports from Persian Gulf countries.  Yanbu, along with the port of Fujairah in the United Arab Emirates, now serves a critical function, carrying a significant share of oil supplies to the global market while bypassing the war zone. Fujairah has previously been attacked, partially halting its operations.  Despite the limited damage, strikes on such key facilities increase the risk of supply disruptions and could further push up global oil prices.

author: United24Media
text: The “Spartan” brigade, together with adjacent units, repelled an enemy assault, destroying a Russian company within 48 hours.  The Russian occupation command committed significant forces to the attack in the Pokrovsky direction, hoping to take advantage of rainy weather. Enemy infantry attempted to advance using cars, motorcycles, and ATVs.  However, “Spartan” and nearby units stopped the attack. In 48 hours, the enemy suffered significant losses, including:  • 120 attack personnel killed; • 6 wounded.  Russian equipment losses included:  • 7 ATVs; • 4 motorcycles; • 3 cars.

author: United24Media
text: Volodymyr Zelenskyy has arrived in France, where he will soon meet with Emmanuel Macron.  “The two leaders will discuss the current situation, France’s support and that of European partners for Ukraine’s defense, as well as ways to increase pressure on Russia, in particular the fight against its shadow fleet,” the Élysée Palace said.

author: United24Media
text: Ukraine finished 7th in the final medal standings at the 2026 Winter Paralympics in Italy.  The Ukrainian national team won 19 medals: 3 gold, 8 silver, and 8 bronze.  Compared with the 2022 Winter Paralympics in Beijing, this is a significant step back. Four years ago, Ukraine won 29 medals, including 10 gold, and finished second behind the host nation.

author: United24Media
text: 🇺🇦🎮🏆 S.T.A.L.K.E.R. 2 has been nominated for the prestigious BAFTA Games Awards 2026.  The Ukrainian shooter is nominated in the Game Beyond Entertainment category of the British award.  This nomination recognizes games that have a significant cultural impact and demonstrate that video games can reflect real-world issues.

author: United24Media
text: The International Criminal Court prosecutor’s office has launched a formal investigation into the Lukashenko regime’s crackdown on protests in 2020–2021.  Belarusian authorities are suspected of committing crimes against humanity, specifically politically motivated deportations carried out as part of state policy.  The ICC prosecutor concluded that the human rights violations were “committed as part of a large-scale and systematic persecution of the civilian population, which, given their scale and the number of victims, was organized in nature,” and were directed against “real or perceived opponents” of self-proclaimed President Alexander Lukashenko.  Belarus is not a member of the ICC, but a case was filed in 2024 by Lithuania, which has ratified the Rome Statute.  The ICC prosecutor’s office established that at least some of the alleged crimes were committed on the territory of Lithuania, where Belarusians were deported, giving the court jurisdiction to consider the case.

text: 📰 Syrian authorities have walked back an announced ban on alcohol in Damascus after outcry from residents and accusations of sectarianism. text: Muslim worshippers across the region gathered to mark the end of Ramadan with Eid prayers on Friday morning. These prayers are one of the most important traditions associated with the festival and take place after dawn, either in a mosque or a public field.  The prayers are distinguished from regular daily prayers because they are accompanied by a sermon, known as a “khutba”. Usually, only Friday prayer services are performed with a sermon.  Amid the ongoing US-Israeli war on Iran, several Gulf countries, including Qatar, Kuwait and the UAE, restricted Eid al-Fitr prayers to mosques, suspending large outdoor gatherings amid heightened tensions linked to the ongoing conflict.  Authorities in the UAE said worshippers should avoid traditional open-air prayer grounds, where large crowds typically gather, “as a precautionary measure”, as governments reassess public safety.  Several countries, including Iran, will celebrate Eid on Saturday.

author: @MiddleEastEye_TG
text: Despite the war and repeated displacement, Noura Abu Ouda has not stopped practising her trade, one deeply intertwined with memories of Eid in the Gaza Strip.  For around ten years, Abu Ouda has worked with a group of women making ka’ak and ma’amoul (traditional filled pastries). The trade typically flourishes during festive seasons, helping to preserve Islamic traditions and the deeply rooted social customs of Gazans.  However, the recent war has imposed a harsh reality on her life. Like many other residents of the Strip, she has faced repeated displacement, forcing her to stop working for extended periods. At other times, she has resorted to using alternative ingredients to continue baking, in an effort to sustain her livelihood and that of the women working alongside her.  “We are trying to preserve our heritage and our traditions, just as we are trying to keep the children’s joy alive with Eid sweets, despite all the difficult circumstances,” Abu Ouda said.
